# How Agent M is developed

**REGISTER**

Agent M uses `scrum-wip`: Scrum with a work-in-progress limit of four items per team and no time box. The model defines the phases, transitions and gates. Each team fills its roles in `docs/role-assignments/<team>.md` from the instance's one participant list, `docs/participants.md`.

## Roles

- Product Owner
- Scrum Master
- Developers

## Practices

- none

## Branches

| Phase or time box | Branch |
|---|---|
| Sprint | `sprint/<team>/<nn>` |

## Definition of Done

The job rules hold for every pull request; no condition is added.

## Sprint close

The Scrum Master closes the sprint with its review, retrospective and decisions on unfinished items. The Product Owner decides the increment's merge into the default branch and must not have written the review or retrospective it checks. The Scrum Master carries out the merge on that recorded decision.

# ITM-1000 Item identifiers take three or more digits

**REGISTER**

## Outcome

MOD-identifiers' Data lets `ITM` take three or more digits. Team 1 took ITM-995 to ITM-999, so no three-digit number is
left. An item `docs/backlog/ITM-1000-*.md` today fails four of MOD-work-plans' taken-over checks: the item file name, the
item read without a problem and the build order in `tests/test_backlog_layout.py`, and the item that names what it
realises in `tests/test_backlog_item_fields.py`. They read through `docs/assets/work-items.mjs`, whose `ITEM_PATH` and
`ITEM_ID` take `ITM-\d{3}` (:29-30), and the build order sorts the identifiers as text, so `ITM-1000` comes before
`ITM-203`.

This item makes MOD-work-plans' taken-over reader and checks take `ITM-<nnn>` with three or more digits, and orders items by
their number, so that ITM-1000 follows ITM-999. This item is the first item with four digits.

## Acceptance

- `docs/assets/work-items.mjs` and `docs/assets/work-items/flow.mjs` take `ITM-<nnn>` with three or more digits, in the
  item file name, the item's id, a sprint's selection and the pull requests that hold a slot of the WIP limit.
- Items are ordered by their number: ITM-203, then ITM-999, then ITM-1000.
- `tests/test_backlog_layout.py`, `tests/test_backlog_item_fields.py`, `tests/test_time_box_selection.py` and
  `tests/parallel_sprints_fixture.py` take three or more digits.
- Counter-proofs: a three-digit item is still read; an `ITM-99` of two digits is still refused.
- The first commit holds only the tests and this item file, and CI is red on it.
- Only the files named above change. The other readers of the three-digit form are later items, one per module.

# ITM-1001 jsrun hands node the code on its standard input

**REGISTER**

## Outcome

`tests/jsrun.py`'s `js` hands node its code as one argument (`node --input-type=module -e <code>`, `:56`).
`repository_findings` in `tests/test_no_history.py` (`:163`) puts the hex of every repository path into that code, about
137,000 bytes. Linux caps one argument at 131,072 bytes (MAX_ARG_STRLEN), so TST-412100 fails there with
`OSError: [Errno 7] Argument list too long: 'node'`, and with it python (2) of every mode=all run. macOS's larger limit
hides it locally. A release cannot run every test while one test cannot start, so the end gates of both teams wait.

This item makes `js` hand node the code on its standard input (`node --input-type=module` with `input=code`). Team 1
measured 300,000 bytes of module code with a top-level `await` run that way. No caller is then bound by an argument limit.

## Acceptance

- `tests/jsrun.py`'s `js` runs node as `node --input-type=module` and gives the code as `input`. Nothing else in the file
  changes, and every caller keeps its interface.
- `tests/test_jsrun_stdin.py` holds TST-1001001 and TST-1001002, declared for MOD-test-document.
  - TST-1001001: `js` of an expression of 300,000 bytes returns its value.
  - TST-1001002, the counter-proof: the same kind of code, longer than `getconf ARG_MAX` and than 131,072 bytes, as the
    argument of `node --input-type=module -e` raises `OSError` with errno E2BIG on Linux and on macOS, and `js` returns
    its value.
- The first commit holds only the test and this item file, and CI is red on it.
- The whole Python suite passes, since every Python test reaches the code of a module through `js`.

# ITM-1002 An agent that is not logged in is shown with its own login step

The draft for this item is accepted (`1c30ad0b` and the acceptances before it); quoted from `main` at 40e04d8d:

# ITM-1003 The Bridge's server tells which origin it is paired with

**REGISTER**

## Outcome

UC-044-install-and-pair-the-bridge.md:81-82 (step 4): "… and tests it; the bridge's window shows *paired with
`<owner>.github.io`*." `serveBridge` returns `{ address, token, close }` and no `pairedWith`
(`src/bridge-http/server.mjs:109`). ITM-1004 shows it in the window.

## The accepted text

Quoted from `main` at 40e04d8d, MOD-bridge-http.md:84-88:

> - `serveBridge(config: { host: string, port: number, origin: string, dataFolder: string, paused: () => boolean }, handlers:
>   BridgeHandlers) -> Promise<{ address: string, token: string, pairedWith: () -> string | null, close: () -> Promise<void>
>   }>` — starts the server, and returns its address and the pairing token in force, made on the first start, for the
>   Bridge's window; `pairedWith()` is the origin of the first request since this start that carried the token in force and
>   came from `origin`, and `null` before one did and again after `pairAnew` (UC-044, pairing). It is kept in memory …

## Acceptance

- Unit tests naming MOD-bridge-http, over a server on `127.0.0.1`: `pairedWith()` is `null` after the start; after a
  request with the token from `origin`, it is that origin; after `pairAnew`, `null` again until the next such request.
- Counter-proofs: a request from another origin, or with a wrong token, leaves it `null`; a restart gives `null` (kept in
  memory only, nothing written to the data folder).
- The first commit holds only the tests, and CI is red on it. No stub is committed.
- Only `src/bridge-http/` and the tests that name MOD-bridge-http change.

# ITM-1005 The Bridge reads its build.json and update key at start

**REGISTER**

## Outcome

MOD-desktop-shell.md:130 and :197-198 have the app read its resources `build.json` and `update-key.pem` at start.
`src/desktop-shell/main.mjs:13-16` reads `--instance`, `--origin` and `--data-folder` from the command line only, and
throws a `TypeError` without `--instance`. So a packaged app started as a person starts it, without arguments, ends at
once. ITM-961's real build (TST-961006) and its tunnel check wait for this item.

## The accepted text

Quoted from `main` at 40e04d8d, MOD-desktop-shell.md:130-136:

> **What the build places among the app's resources**, read at start:
>
> - `build.json` — `{ "instance": "alice/agent-m", "appId": "io.github.alice.agent-m.bridge", "origin":
>   "https://alice.github.io", "version": "2026.10.0", "commit": "<commit>" }`: the instance whose release this is, the
>   app's identifier, the instance's Pages origin — the one origin the API answers across origins —, the version and its
>   commit.
> - `update-key.pem` — the publisher's public update key, Ed25519, in PEM.

## Acceptance

- Unit tests naming MOD-desktop-shell: started without arguments, over a fixture resources folder holding `build.json` and
  `update-key.pem`, the app serves the Bridge with `origin` from `build.json` and its data folder from the instance; the
  update check uses the key from `update-key.pem`.
- A missing or unreadable `build.json` ends the start with an error naming the file, and nothing is served.
- Counter-proof: an `origin` taken from anywhere but `build.json` fails the first test.
- Whether the command-line options stay, for tests, is the developer's reading of the accepted text, named in the pull
  request; the text names only the resources.
- The first commit holds only the tests, and CI is red on it. No stub is committed.
- Only `src/desktop-shell/` and the tests that name MOD-desktop-shell change.

# ITM-1010 A closed sprint holds no item that its change already brought to the default branch

**REGISTER**

## Outcome

Since ITM-269's pull request #949 was merged into `sprint/team1/93`, `heldItems` counts ITM-269 as held by team 2's closed
sprints 16 and 24, which selected it in October and whose change reached `main` on 2026-10-09 (team2/16.md:41, :182). No
pull request title of theirs named ITM-269. SPEC.md:1672-1674 holds an item "until its change is merged into the default
branch or the item returns to the backlog". `conflicts` then held every MOD-settings-pages and MOD-product-process item of
team 1 back against "ITM-269".

**First task:** read how `heldItems` tells that a sprint's change reached the default branch, and name the record that
would show it for a sprint whose pull requests do not name the item.

## Acceptance

- A closed sprint whose increment reached the default branch holds none of its items, whichever later pull request names
  them. A test with a fixture of two sprints shows it, with a counter-proof.
- The first commit holds only the tests, and CI is red on it. No stub is committed.

# ITM-1025 A job running in another browser's tab is listed with its record and that note

**REGISTER**

## Outcome

UC-036-inspect-running-jobs.md:136-137 (1b): "A job was started in another browser and runs in its tab. Its record is
listed, with the note that its live state and log exist only in that tab". On `main` such a job is shown *ended without
record*: `src/runtimes/index.mjs:84` gives `known: false` for a tab job this tab does not hold, and
`src/job-ledger/states.mjs:20` turns that into *ended without record* (1c).

## The accepted text

The draft for this item is accepted (`1c30ad0b` and the acceptances before it); quoted from `main` at 40e04d8d:

MOD-runtimes.md:196-199:

> host's `readHistory` (`changes: false`), whose date is after the record's `## End` of state `cancelled`. A job of the tab
>   route that another browser took — its `## Taken` names another browser than this one (MOD-job-ledger) — gives
>   `reachable: false` with the reason that its live state and log exist only in that browser's tab (UC-036 1b); one this
>   browser took and this tab does not hold gives `known: false`, so that it is *ended without record* (1c).

## Acceptance

- A tab job whose `## Taken` names another browser is listed with `reachable: false`, the note that its live state and
  log exist only in that browser's tab, and the folded explanation of ITM-1078. A tab job this browser took and this tab
  no longer holds is *ended without record*. A `## Taken` of bare `tab` is read as this browser's. Each with a
  counter-proof. Whether another browser's tab has since closed cannot be known here, so such a job stays
  `reachable: false`.

## Not ready: its draft waits

No accepted text says how MOD-runtimes learns this browser's identifier (sprint 96, developer-sonnet-i's stop). The
draft for MOD-runtimes is described in 96.md: the tab's route reads `browser` from the store of the instance its Pages
address names, and makes it at first use. It goes to akmaier once it is reviewed, and after akmaier has decided team 1's
pending draft `c3ec9099` on the same file. The item is built only once the draft is accepted.
- The first commit holds only the tests, and CI is red on it. No stub is committed.

## For akmaier, from the review of the draft (opus reviewer, sprint 96)

The accepted texts raise three points that the draft does not settle. They go to akmaier with it:
- **SPEC.md:1790-1791**, the check of PROGRESS AND JOB STATE ARE DERIVED, NOT STORED: "Deleting all local storage and
  reloading shows the same progress and the same job states." With `browser` in `localStorage`, deleting it makes this
  browser's earlier tab jobs read as another browser's. They are then `reachable: false`, not *ended without record*.
  The derivation is unchanged, but the shown state of those jobs differs.
- **Export and import.** `exportSettings` (MOD-browser-store.md:121) carries every setting, so `browser` reaches a second
  browser, and two browsers then share one identifier. A possible item: leave `browser` out of the export, as tab values
  are.
- **Two tabs of one browser.** A job running in a second tab of this browser is read here as one this browser took and
  this tab does not hold, so *ended without record* (MOD-runtimes at `26dac0e5`, :199). This is unchanged by the draft.

# ITM-1138 The pages of roles, process, releases and settings read the repository they show once per load

**REGISTER**

## Outcome

SPEC.md:672: "one load of a dashboard page reads its commit and that commit's tree once". With a token, `#roles`,
`#process`, `#release` and `#settings` read the same commit and tree three or four times. Their Check
(`tests/load-per-view.test.mjs`) covers only the start page, `#arc`, `#spec` and `#backlog`.

**Where the Hosts are made, and why the tree is read again** (read on `a3973660`):
- The app reads the shown repository once (`src/site-frame/dashboard-app.mjs:255`, `loadSnapshot`).
- For the review pages, `pagesHost()` (`dashboard-app.mjs:576-614`) wraps the host, so a `readSnapshot` during the load
  gets that snapshot back. `reviewContext()` (`:637-643`) gives `product: null` for the instance.
- The four pages instead get a new Host for the product and one for the instance on each load, `product` never null:
  `#settings` at `:754-756`, `#release` at `:800-801`, `#roles` and `#process` in the adapters
  `docs/assets/dashboard/roles-view.mjs:18-21` and `process-view.mjs:27-30`. Each route calls `readSnapshot` on both
  (`src/implementation-pages/roles.mjs:76-78`, `process.mjs:121-123`, `src/settings-pages/settings.mjs:945`, `:956`,
  `:862-863`).
- `src/test-pages/release.mjs` reads the product's snapshot twice through the same host, in `pendingCandidate`
  (`:138-141`) and `paintForm` (`:158-163`), even for a product that is not the instance.
- A Host keeps no snapshot: MOD-repository-hosts.md:84-85, "It keeps nothing beyond that".

**What the accepted texts already ask.**
- MOD-site-frame.md:242-243: "the default branch of the repository a route shows, asked once per page, and its snapshot
  there".
- MOD-site-frame.md:145-146: "the empty `product` names the instance itself".

So the fix fits the texts as they stand, and needs no draft:
- The frame gives these routes the context it gives the review pages: the wrapped host, and `product: null` for the
  instance.
- The routes take `product ?? instance` where they now dereference `product.host`.
- `paintForm` takes what `pendingCandidate` read.
- `#settings` is shown before the load's snapshot is read (`dashboard-app.mjs:849-853`), so it waits for it.
- The frame's wrapper matches `ref === T.ref`, while the routes ask for `info.defaultBranch`. Read first whether the two
  agree for every product (AGENTS.md §6a.1).

It builds on ITM-681, which removes the adapters of `#roles` and `#process`, so those routes are shown by the frame
directly.

## Acceptance

- `tests/load-per-view.test.mjs` also loads `#roles`, `#process`, `#release` and `#settings`, for the instance and for a
  product that is another repository. Each sends its commit and tree once. `#process` may additionally read the commit
  its declaration names, when that is another commit. Counter-proof: a route that connects a host of its own exceeds
  that count.
- The first commit holds only the tests, and CI is red on it. No stub is committed.

**REGISTER**

## Outcome

ITM-1084 found the cause of `ENOTEMPTY` when a test removes its temporary repositories. A push, a commit or a fetch starts

is part of this item.

## Failure path and evidence boundary

At `87c4f1f8`, `testEndpoint` calls `requestFor` and then `providerRequest`, whose OpenAI-compatible body omits
`stream`. An HTTP-success response is read by `response.json()` before `exchangeAnswer`. A response beginning
with SSE `data:` fails JSON parsing; the catch returns `works: false` with the parser message diagnosed as

The failure node is the negotiated response format, not proof that the server could not be reached.

The retained controlled diagnostic supplied with the refinement assignment has a JSON positive: the public test
returns `works: true` and the ordinary driver returns the literal `Known answer.`. With the constructed SSE-default
reply, the public test makes one intercepted request and returns `works: false`, `not reachable`, with the

The assignment also records that NVIDIA's hosted reference defaults `stream` to true and supports false; the
implementation report names the exact official provider reference it uses, without a paid call.

The separate credential-free browser-origin comparison recorded by the Scrum Master found NHR's required
cross-origin permission and no required Access-Control-Allow-Origin header on NVIDIA's response. Explicit JSON
negotiation does not grant CORS permission. UC-003's browser-refusal diagnosis and existing Bridge alternative remain
unchanged; this item makes no claim that live NVIDIA becomes callable directly from Chrome.

# ITM-1182 The tunnel check's test SSH server takes only a host key it can parse, and leaves nothing open when it fails

**REGISTER**

## Outcome

node (11) of #1301 at `c3f8abbd` was cancelled at the job's two minutes. It did not run out of margin: it failed, then
hung. Read from the full job log 120056351279:
- line 422, 20:01:45: `node --test` starts;
- lines 480-497, 20:01:52: TST-961005 (`tests/bridge-build-build-platform.test.mjs:340`) fails with
  `Cannot parse privateKey: Malformed OpenSSH private key`, raised by ssh2's `new Server` (`server.js:249`) from
  `testSshServer` (`src/bridge-build/check.mjs:134`), called by `tunnelCheck` (`check.mjs:187`) from `buildPlatform`
  (`builder.mjs:220`);
- lines 499-512, 20:01:55: tests 11 to 13 pass;
- line 517, 20:04:09: "The operation was canceled." Nothing is written for 2 min 14 s before it.

**The path.**
1. `check.mjs:131` starts the answer web server (`answer.listen`).
2. `check.mjs:134` builds the SSH server with a fresh `utils.generateKeyPairSync("ed25519").private` as host key.
3. ssh2 cannot parse some of the keys it generates itself. On this machine 13 of 3000 calls of
   `new Server({ hostKeys: [utils.generateKeyPairSync("ed25519").private] })` threw that error (ssh2 from
   `src/bridge-build/node_modules`).
4. `testSshServer` throws before it returns its `close`. In `tunnelCheck`, `server` stays null, so the `finally`
   (`check.mjs:216-220`) closes nothing, and the answer server from step 1 stays listening.
5. The open server, by this reading, keeps the test file's process alive, and the shard waits for it until the job's limit
   cancels it. That step is read from the code and the 2 min 14 s of silence, not shown by a run.

So about one call in 230 fails TST-961005 and blocks a node shard, on any pull request, whatever it changes.

**The existing pattern.** `src/tunnels/index.mjs:41-45` generates the bridge's own key the same way, and keeps generating
until `matchedPair` (which parses both halves with `utils.parseKey`) accepts the pair. The tunnel check's host key does
not.

## Acceptance

- `testSshServer` uses only a host key that ssh2 parses, following `src/tunnels/index.mjs:41-45`.
- When building the SSH server fails, `testSshServer` closes what it already opened, and the tunnel check fails with
  `TunnelCheckFailed` instead of hanging.
- A unit test hands the check an ssh2 whose key generation gives an unparseable key first. The check either succeeds with
  the next key, or fails, and in both cases the test's process exits. Counter-proof: today's `check.mjs` fails it.
- The first commit holds only the tests, and CI is red on it.

# ITM-1183 A node shard rerun alone installs xvfb and openbox on a cache miss

**REGISTER**

## Outcome

ITM-1179 (#1304, #1305) has the job `apt-archives` download xvfb and openbox into an Actions cache. Every node shard
`needs` it, restores that cache, and installs from it. A shard rerun alone does not run `apt-archives` again. When its
restore finds no cache, its install fails before any test.

**The path, read on `sprint/team2/103` at `3ed501f9`** (`.github/workflows/tests.yml`):
1. `:103-107`, the shard's step "Restore the downloaded archives of xvfb and openbox" restores
   `/home/runner/apt-archives` by key `apt-xvfb-openbox-<os>-<week>`.
2. `:108-113`, "Install xvfb and openbox" runs `apt-get install` with
   `Dir::Cache::archives=/home/runner/apt-archives`. It does not create the folder or its `partial` subfolder. Only
   `apt-archives` does that, at `:81`.
3. On a miss the folder is absent, and apt stops.

**Shown on job 120054035567** (node (0) alone, attempt 3 of run 39842730231):
- line 155, 19:56:42: `Cache not found for input keys: apt-xvfb-openbox-Linux-2026-43, apt-xvfb-openbox-Linux-`;
- line 204: `E: Archives directory /home/runner/apt-archives/partial is missing.`;
- line 205: exit code 100.

**Open: why the cache was missing.** The same run's `apt-archives` had saved that key in attempt 1 (job 120047836731,
line 753, `Cache saved with key: apt-xvfb-openbox-Linux-2026-43`). The repository's caches were deleted shortly before,
to measure #1305's cold run 39844719741, created at 19:58:12. Whether that deletion caused this miss is not shown. Either
way, a shard must not depend on the cache being there.

**What #1306 (ITM-1184) already does.** `tests.yml`'s node shard creates `apt-archives/partial` and
`apt-lists/partial`, and on a miss it runs `apt-get update` and installs from the mirror (`cfafeb06`). Still missing:
a test that pins this, and a single-shard rerun after a cache miss shown green on CI
(`docs/gates/20261022-2102-development-release-testing-30d9.md`, "Open").

The remedy until this item is done: rerun the whole workflow, not one shard.

## Acceptance

- A node shard whose restore finds no cache still installs xvfb and openbox, within its two minutes, and on a hit it
  fetches nothing.
- `nightly.yml`, where it runs these tests, holds the same.
- A test of MOD-test-schedule states both for the two workflows. Counter-proof: today's install step, without the folder,
  fails it.
- Shown on CI: one shard rerun alone after the cache is removed is green, with its time from the jobs API.
- The first commit holds only the tests, and CI is red on it.

# ITM-312 A local clone as a repository host

**REGISTER**

## Outcome

MOD-repository-hosts' adapter for a local clone, `local-git.mjs`, as its file states it, in Node only. `connect(address,
{ clone })` gives a host whose `readSnapshot` reads the clone at a branch, a tag or a commit, first fetching a commit
the clone lacks from its origin with the clone's own credentials — `NotFound` when the origin lacks it too —; whose
`commitFiles` commits all files in one commit on a branch and pushes only when the push fast-forwards, else `Moved` with

  folder as the origin and a clone of it, which is not the network: a snapshot at a branch with its paths and a file's
  text; a commit the clone lacks fetched from the origin, and one the origin lacks `NotFound`; two files committed and
  pushed in one commit while the origin's branch stands at the expected head; `Moved`, with nothing pushed, after
  another commit landed first; a file holding a configured secret refused by its path; a pull request through the

# ITM-477 An active GitHub token is refused by the desktop dashboard

**REGISTER**

## Outcome

The desktop dashboard's repository-token Test uses the intended stored credential in its request to that token's own
repository server, and the reported active-token rejection is resolved at its demonstrated failure node. This item
does not assume that the token expired, that the desktop holds the same bytes as the iPhone, or that the rejection is
a rate limit. The human reports that the token remains active until the end of December and works in an older iPhone
version. The current Chrome Test follows the public HostError TokenRefused path, which MOD-repository-hosts maps from
HTTP 401; the actual request's credential and response have not yet been compared with the working version.

ITM-475 fixes the independently reproduced non-credential failure recording and unsupported expiry wording. Neither
fix establishes the cause of this live rejection. Candidate ownership is MOD-settings-pages and MOD-repository-hosts;
an existing composition caller is added to the assigned scope only if the data-flow evidence establishes its part.

## Acceptance

- Read the existing working caller before probing. Trace the stored setting through credential selection, request
  construction and the server response, naming actual and expected data at the failure node without recording secrets.
- Establish a known-positive request with the same repository and the intended credential before treating a negative
  comparison as a finding. Preserve the distinction between human-reported iPhone behavior and measured desktop behavior.
- Write the regression at the demonstrated failure node before production edits, obtain its failing CI result, and
  record its planted-fault and restored-pass counterproof. Independent release tests guard the repaired behavior.
- Verify the deployed main-branch dashboard's harmless Test after the fix, reporting its actual result without
  substituting a fixture pass for successful live authentication.
- Keep the credential hidden outside an expressly authorized inspection; never place it in repository evidence,
  output, a URL, or a request to another server. A denied clipboard comparison is not retried through another route.

## Intake Decision

Independent Product Owner po-sol permits registration only. The item remains unselected and has no implementation
job. The human expressly approves the specific one-request clipboard comparison after the earlier denial. This does
not authorize another credential transfer, token replacement or a request to another destination.

## Authorized Diagnostic Measurement

At 2026-10-15T17:46:57.434Z, one GET to https://api.github.com/repos/akmaier/agent-m through Agent M's existing public
connect/parseAddress/repositoryInfo interface in Node returns HTTP 401 and HostError TokenRefused. Request ID:
FF95:2B36EB:1FC3B53:2FB66B2:6AD11191. The probe uses the desktop field's stored value unchanged and permits only that
single request, with redirects refused. No rate-limit headers are present. No token is printed, saved or put in a URL;
the field is concealed and the originally empty clipboard is restored and verified empty after the request.

Data flow: settings.mjs:447-449 binds stored.value to the field -> public Host connect -> github.mjs:58 constructs
Bearer authorization -> github.mjs:141 repositoryInfo -> failures.mjs:45 fetch -> failures.mjs:98 maps 401 to
TokenRefused. The earlier controlled 200 comparison of the old and current callers verifies the harness's positive
path, not this credential's live validity. Chrome is not the sole location of the rejection. Expiry, equality with the
iPhone value and the actual cause remain unproved; no successful live intended-credential control or fix is claimed.

## Transport Audit And Controlled Reproduction

At 2026-10-15 18:02 UTC, the requested follow-up diagnostic discovers that the current Chrome extension's session
clipboard and the system clipboard are different: the session contains the 93-character field value in the expected
token format, while the system clipboard contains 32 characters, whitespace and no expected token prefix. The Node
probe refuses that input before any network request. The session clipboard is restored. No value is printed or saved.

The earlier 17:46 measurement checked the system value's prefix but did not compare its full identity with the browser
field. Its HTTP 401 remains the observed result, but its assertion that the exact browser value was tested outside
Chrome is not established by the saved evidence. It must not be used to exclude a browser-path problem. The current
clipboard mismatch does not establish what either clipboard contained during the earlier request.

The public Host's 200 positive control and 401 mapping pass in the same diagnostic process. A direct attempt there
returns Unreachable without an HTTP response. A private local handoff to a network-enabled Node probe is refused before
credential transfer; that process is stopped and its unused socket removed. No GitHub response body is obtained by
these attempts. Native Chrome Network-panel inspection is blocked by auto-review pending specific human approval;
that approval is requested, with authentication-header exposure identified as the risk. No native-inspection
alternative is used after the denial.

The existing dashboard-product-store-migration test file passes all seven tests. An additional in-memory probe uses
the existing public createStore and productStore callers, not real credentials. Its legacy-only positive control gives
the same value to both callers and removes the migrated duplicate. With deliberately different legacy and populated
canonical entries, createStore.getToken selects the legacy value, while productStore.getToken selects the canonical
value and leaves the conflicting legacy entry in place. The path is product-store-adapter.mjs:74 -> copyToken:45-47
(do not overwrite a populated canonical entry) -> getToken:115 (read the canonical entry). This reproduces a possible
version-dependent selection, not the state of the live browser or iPhone. No production fix or live cause is claimed.

## Reported Login Dependency And Live Positive

The human reports that the token is accepted while logged into github.com in the browser and rejected otherwise.
This is the human's reproduction condition, not a measured comparison of identical outgoing requests. It does not
establish that GitHub's token API requires a browser session, or that a conflicting stored credential is present.

At 2026-10-15T18:20:20.232Z the agent runs the deployed dashboard's existing Settings -> Repositories -> Test once.
The page reports "The repository token is working" and records a successful test at that time; the repository line
shows main at 13a09de77095 and the product metadata loads. The token remains concealed, its displayed expiry remains

The caller path is settings.mjs:497 (read the saved setting) -> settings.mjs:504 (public repositoryInfo) ->

No authentication implementation job starts, no code fix is claimed, and no token rotation or login change is needed

**Read at sprint team1/93 (developer-sonnet-c): nothing to build.** It records an incident that did not reproduce, and

# ITM-486 The runner offers a kind's tools to its drafter and carries out their calls

**REGISTER**

## Outcome

Where a kind names tools, MOD-job-runner gives the drafter of each exchange a `ToolUse` — only to a model endpoint
that declares *use tools*, only the tools whose capability it declares and that the page's subject does not refuse — and
carries out each call through the tool's strategy: `list-files`, `read-file` and `search-files` at the commit the job
read, refusing a path `places.contents` names for a restricted source that does not allow the drafter's place;
`propose-edit`, which holds a document's new text in the draft's `edits` and refuses every file its module file names;
and `hand-over`, which holds a proposed hand-over in the draft's `handOver` and queues nothing. Proposed edits are
checked in the round as every drafted document is.

It builds against MOD-job-runner's file as accepted at `4345829a`: the tools offered leave out those the job's
parameter `refuses` names.

What the module file leaves unstated, and what is built:
- **Who gets a `ToolUse`.** A drafter whose type is `model endpoint` and that declares *use tools*, for a kind that names
  tools; every other drafter gets `null`.
  - Its `definitions` are the kind's tools in the kind's order, read with MOD-job-catalogue's `toolsOf`, less every tool
    whose capability the drafter does not declare and every tool `refuses` names. A missing `refuses` names none.
  - Its `limit` is the kind's `toolLimit`.
- **A call's arguments.** They are checked against the tool's argument schema with the validator the runner already
  reads a draft by (`misfit`, `src/job-runner/loop.mjs`). A tool not offered is answered `refused: <name> is not offered here`, and arguments the schema refuses
  are answered `refused: <what the validator names>`.
- **`list-files`.** The paths of the product's snapshot under `folder`, one per line, in order.
- **`read-file`.** The file's text, or `refused: no file <path>`.
- **`search-files`.** Each line of the product's files holding `text`, as `<path>:<line number>: <line>`.
- **A restricted path.** A path `places.contents` names for a source whose allowed places do not include the drafter's
  is answered `refused: <path> holds content of <source>, which may not go to <place>`. A missing `contents` names none.
- **`propose-edit`.** A path in `docs/` is held in the draft's `edits` as `{ path, text }`, the later of two edits of one
  path replacing the earlier. It is refused, naming where the document is changed, for:
  - `SPEC.md`, under `docs/use-cases/` and under `docs/architecture/`;
  - every record under `docs/approvals/`, `docs/gates/`, `docs/jobs/`, `docs/conversations/`, `docs/test-results/` and
    `docs/tests/`;
  - every change queue under `docs/spec-freigaben/`;
  - `docs/settings.md`, `docs/collaborators.md` and `docs/conversation-recording.md`;
  - every path outside `docs/`.
- **`hand-over`.** It holds `{ kind, works_on, task }` in the draft's `handOver`. A kind the catalogue does not hold, or
  one without a participant, is refused. The participant and the route are the bar's (ITM-505).
- **What a call returns.** One text, which the participant reads. Nothing is written by any tool.

No existing test's expected result changes, release tests included. The tests of `prepareJob` and `runJob` use kinds
that name no tools, whose drafters get `tools: null`, and no test compares a whole `DriverInput`. Model endpoints use the
tools from ITM-488 on, so `endpointDriver` is not changed here.

## Acceptance

- Each built-in tool answers a fixture call as the module file says, a refusal naming why; a tool not offered, or
  arguments its schema refuses, is answered with a refusal the participant reads.
- A coding agent gets `null`; a drafter without *use tools* gets no tool; `limit` is the kind's `tool_limit`.
- Nothing is written by any tool; a component test runs a fixture drafter that reads, proposes an edit and a hand-over.

# ITM-488 A model endpoint works in a tool loop

**REGISTER**

## Outcome

Where a `DriverInput` carries `tools`, `endpointDriver` offers their definitions, hands each call the endpoint makes
to `tools.call`, returns its result, and goes on until the endpoint answers without a call — at most `tools.limit` calls,
then once more without tools; the usage is the sum of what each request reported. Each request is one
`endpointExchange`.

What the module file leaves unstated, and what is built:
- **Without tools.** Where the input carries no `tools`, or a `ToolUse` with no definitions, `send` makes the one request it
  makes today. Nothing changes there.
- **The messages.**
  - They begin with the person's turn, `driverPrompt(input)`.
  - After each answer with calls, they gain the assistant's turn with its text and calls, and then one turn of role
    `tool` per call, with its `callId` and the text `tools.call` returned.
  - Each request is `endpointExchange(config, { messages, tools: tools.definitions })`.
- **The limit.** Calls are carried out one by one, in the order the endpoint made them, until `tools.limit` calls have
  been carried out.
  - A call of the same answer beyond the limit is answered with the tool text `refused: the limit of <n> tool calls is
    reached`, since the endpoint expects a result for each call.
  - Then one request follows with `tools: []`, and its text is the answer.
- **The usage.** The sum of each field over the requests that reported usage. It is `null` when none did.
- **A cancel.** `endpointExchange` takes no signal, so the driver checks `options.signal` before each request and before
  each call, and aborts there with the abort error `send` throws today. A request already sent is not cut off.
- **A failure.** An `EndpointFailed` of any request ends `send` with it, and no request is repeated.

No existing test's expected result changes, release tests included. The tests of `endpointDriver`
(`tests/endpoint-driver.test.mjs`, `tests/endpoint-driver-release-21.test.mjs`, `tests/runtimes-tab.test.mjs`) send no
tools, and `endpointExchange`'s tests are unchanged.

## Acceptance

- A fixture endpoint that calls two tools and then answers yields that answer, the two calls carried out in order,
  and the summed usage; at the limit, one request without tools follows.
- A cancel through the signal aborts the loop; a failed request is not repeated.
- The first commit holds only the tests, and CI is red on it.
- Each test states its expected values in its own text (`A TEST DOES NOT TAKE ITS EXPECTED RESULT FROM A DOCUMENT`); an
  existing test that the change turns red is not changed here: the Developer stops and names it.

# ITM-505 A hand-over is shown, queued on the person's click and followed

**REGISTER**

## Outcome

A hand-over the participant proposed is shown with its kind, what it works on, its task, the participant with its
place and its route from `routesFor`; *Hand over* queues it with `handOverJob` only where `startable` and `holdsRole` let a
kind of the product's workflow start, showing the reasons otherwise; the bar follows the job by its record and
`liveState` until it ends — *waiting for GitHub Actions* with the run's address, or for the Bridge —, shows its log's
answer and its commits, and *Stop* cancels it with `cancelJob`.

**The readings, settled at sprint team1/50's start** from MOD-prompt-bar (Interfaces, `startPromptBar`), MOD-work-plans'
`startable` and the code it builds on:
- **What is shown.** The proposal's kind, what it works on, its task, the participant with its processing place
  (`placeOf`), and the route `routesFor` gives, or its reason where none is offered. *Hand over* is offered beside it.
- **When the start rules apply.** They apply where the hand-over works on an item or a step of the product's plan, that
  is, one that `productFacts(… { scope: "work" })` lists among `plan.states`. For each such item, the bar asks
  `startable(item, plan.states, context)`. The context holds:
  - the workflow from the facts;
  - the role assignment and the running sprint of the team whose sprint selects the item, or `null` for both where none
    does;
  - `held`, and the work-in-progress limit from the facts;
  - `participants: [the proposed participant]`.

  With that one participant, `startable`'s own check of "no holder of the implementing role in `assignment` with what the
  role needs" is the check that this participant holds the implementing role. It is made with `holdsRole`
  (`src/work-plans/states.mjs:229–243`), so the bar repeats no rule of the work plans. Any reason is shown, and nothing is
  queued.
- **Queuing.** Only on a person's click (`event.isTrusted`), `handOverJob(prepared, route, start, host, head, task,
  target)` is called, as `src/runtimes/hand-over.mjs:49` takes it. The head is the one the facts were read at.
- **Following.** After the hand-over, the bar reads the product's default branch every 15 seconds until the job has
  ended, and lists the job's row with `listJobs` and `liveState`. Fifteen seconds keeps one followed job within a few
  hundred requests an hour, under GitHub's 5,000.
  - On CI it shows *waiting for GitHub Actions* with the run's address, which `jobLog` gives as `{ address }`.
  - On a Bridge it shows the lines `jobLog`'s stream yields, as they come.
  - Once the record has its end, it shows the end's state and the commits it names, and stops following.
- ***Stop*** while it is followed calls `cancelJob`, and shows `cancelled` or `cancelling` as it answers.
- **The Bridges** are handed to the runtimes from their stored entries with `settingsOf` and `bridgeAt`, as the bar
  already does for a message.

**Existing test whose expected result changes:** TST-600030 (`tests/prompt-bar.test.mjs:418`), which expects no button
*Hand over*. UC-019's TST-377013 (S12) then holds as well. It stays `todo` until a developer who implements none of this
item turns it plain.

## Acceptance

- With fixtures, a hand-over refused for each reason names it and queues nothing; an allowed one is queued on the click
  only, followed to its end, and cancelled by *Stop*.

- in a clone, with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`.
A commit the server does not know is not contained. It crosses the network and fails as `readSnapshot` fails. It is the
fact a caller hands MOD-work-plans' `heldItems` as `onDefault` (ITM-516).

What the module file leaves unstated, and what is built. The Developer confirms each request against the server's
documentation and names the page in the pull request.
- **GitHub.** `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/{commit}...{branch}`. The branch holds the commit when the answer's
  `behind_by` is 0, which GitHub reports as status `ahead` or `identical`. A 404 or 422 for an unknown commit is not
  contained.
- **GitLab.** `GET /projects/:id/repository/merge_base?refs[]={commit}&refs[]={branch}`. The branch holds the commit when
  the merge base's `id` is the commit. A 404 or 400 for an unknown commit is not contained.
- **A clone.** `git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit> <branch>`. Exit 0 is contained, exit 1 is not, and any other exit —
  an unknown commit — is not contained.
- **The request.** It is a read with the repository's own token, through the adapter's existing request helper and origin
  gate. No new `fetch` is added.

No existing test's expected result changes, release tests included; no test lists a host's functions.

## Acceptance

- Unit tests name MOD-repository-hosts and state, before the code exists, against fixture servers and a fixture clone:
  - a commit on the branch is contained;

  - an unknown commit is not;
  - a refused token is `TokenRefused`, and a used-up limit `RateLimited`;
  - the request carries the token only to its own server.
- The first commit holds only these tests, and CI is red on it. Every new test's counter-proof is recorded in the pull
  request.

# ITM-526 The access test is not raced by git's own lock files

**REGISTER**

## Outcome

TST-472076 ("testAccess — nothing is changed in any clone", `tests/bridge-jobs-access.test.mjs`) measures a clone before
and after with `stateOf`, which walks it with `readdirSync` and then calls `statSync` on each entry. Git's background
maintenance creates and removes `.git/objects/maintenance.lock` on its own. When the file vanishes between the two calls,
`statSync` throws `ENOENT` and the test fails, though testAccess changed nothing. This happened on #559's first CI
attempt.

The walk leaves out git's own transient lock files. Every other file is measured as before, so a change that testAccess
made still fails the test.

What the item leaves to be built, and the value:
- **Which files are left out.** A file below a clone's `.git/` whose name ends in `.lock` is git's own lock. It is not
  measured.
- **Any other file that vanishes between the two calls.** It still fails the test.

TST-472076's expected result does not change, release tests included. Only how it measures its fixture changes, which
`AN IMPLEMENTATION JOB CHANGES ONLY ITS MODULES` allows for an existing test.

## Acceptance

- `stateOf` leaves out `.git/**/*.lock`. A planted `.git/objects/maintenance.lock` that vanishes between `readdirSync` and
  `statSync` no longer makes the walk throw.
  - Counter-proof: without the exclusion, the same plant throws `ENOENT`.
  - Second counter-proof: a file outside `.git/` that testAccess would change still fails TST-472076.
- Only `tests/bridge-jobs-access.test.mjs` changes, and MOD-bridge-jobs' code does not.
- The test's values stay in its own text (`A TEST DOES NOT TAKE ITS EXPECTED RESULT FROM A DOCUMENT`).

The readings, settled from MOD-runtimes' Data and from GitLab's documentation (docs.gitlab.com, "CI/CD inputs", read
2026-10-16):
- **Where the inputs are declared.** "Inputs for pipelines must be defined in the `spec:inputs` header of the main
  `.gitlab-ci.yml` file."
  - The `.gitlab-ci.yml` that `jobWorkflowFiles` writes therefore starts with a `spec:` header that declares `job`,
    `task` and `endpoint`, each with `default: ""`. GitLab says: "If any input is missing a default, the pipeline fails
    when it triggers automatically", and a push starts this pipeline without inputs.
  - After the header's `---`, the file includes `.gitlab/agent-m-jobs.yml` with `inputs:`, passing each of the three on
    as `$[[ inputs.<name> ]]` ("Use `include:inputs` to set the values for inputs when the included configuration is
    added to the pipeline").
- **The included file.** `src/runtimes/workflow/gitlab.yml` starts with the same `spec:` header and `---`. Each job sets
  the variables `AGENT_M_INPUT_JOB`, `AGENT_M_INPUT_TASK` and `AGENT_M_INPUT_ENDPOINT`, each to `$[[ inputs.<name> ]]` as
  the whole value. An input that is a whole value is "interpolated into the configuration as its specified type", so a
  task with quotes or line breaks stays one string. The task goes into a variable of the job, never into a file (MOD-
  runtimes, Data: "the task is given to the job and written to no file").
- **The source.** GitLab names a pipeline that the pipelines API created by `CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE` `api`. MOD-runtimes'
  table runs `onDispatch` both for "a start from the server's own page" (`web`) and "from a hand-over" (the API). So the
  one rule of `onDispatch` becomes `$CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "web" || $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "api"`. Each entry keeps
  exactly one rule.

One existing test's expected result changes: TST-472723 (`tests/runtimes-workflow.test.mjs`). It expects `.gitlab-ci.yml`
to be only the `include:`. TST-472724, which expects one rule for each entry that includes `$CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE ==
"web"` for `onDispatch`, holds as it is. TST-472727, which expects every variable the GitLab file reads to be
predefined or Agent M's own, holds too, since `$[[ inputs.… ]]` is not a variable.

## Acceptance

- `jobWorkflowFiles("gitlab", …)` writes a `.gitlab-ci.yml` whose `spec:` declares the three inputs with an empty
  default, and which passes them to the included file.
- The included file declares the same three inputs, and gives each job the three `AGENT_M_INPUT_…` variables.
- `onDispatch` runs for the sources `web` and `api`.
- The variables test of the GitLab file still finds only predefined variables and Agent M's own.
- The first commit holds only the tests, and CI is red on it.
- Each test states its expected values in its own text.

# ITM-535 A job's live state, its log and its cancel

**REGISTER**

## Outcome

MOD-runtimes' `liveState`, `jobLog` and `cancelJob`, as its file states them. None is built yet
(`src/runtimes/index.mjs`). ITM-505, which follows a handed-over job until it ends, builds on them.

Which CI run belongs to a job, settled from the texts. MOD-job-ledger's Data says a record's `## Taken` holds "`by:` the
route that took it — a CI run's address, a Bridge's name, this tab". MOD-workflow-entries writes that address when it takes
a job: `takeJob(…, job.runUrl …)` in `src/workflow-entries/product.mjs`, with `runUrl` built from `GITHUB_RUN_ID`. So:
- **A job no runtime has taken yet.** No `## Taken` part. Its `liveState` is `{ reachable: true, known: false, running:
  false, cancelling: false, log: null, usage: null, writtenAfterCancel: [] }`. `cancelJob` ends it at once with the end
  `cancelled`, and returns `cancelled`.
- **A job taken on CI.** `taken.by` is the run's address. The run is the `CiRun` among `listCiRuns({ workflow })` whose
  `url` is that address; `workflow` is the job workflow's file name (`agent-m-jobs.yml` on GitHub, as `handOverJob`
  names it).
  - `liveState` is `running` while the run's state is `queued`, `running` or `waiting`. `log` is the run's address, and
    `usage` is `null`, since a run reports none until the job's end.
  - `jobLog` gives `{ address }`, the run's address.
  - `cancelJob` asks `cancelCiRun(run.id)`, then reads the run once. Where it is `cancelled`, it appends the end
    `cancelled` and returns `cancelled`; otherwise it returns `cancelling` and appends nothing.
  - A run not found is `{ reachable: true, known: false, … }`.
  - A failure of the host gives `reachable: false` and its reason, never an error.
- **A job taken on a Bridge.** It is ITM-545's, cut off at sprint 45. MOD-bridge-client's `bridgeJobs`, `bridgeJobLog`
  and `cancelOnBridge`, which it needs, are not built yet (ITM-544). Here such a job's `liveState` is `{ reachable: false,
  reason: "the Bridge's jobs are not read yet", known: false, … }`, and its `jobLog` and `cancelJob` give the same reason
  as a `RuntimeError` named `NotSupported`.
- **A job taken by this tab.** `runOnTab` keeps the abort of each job it runs with a record, by the record's id, until
  the job ends.
  - `liveState` is `running` while the tab holds the job, and `known: false` for a job this tab does not run.
  - `jobLog` is `{ gone: true }`, since the tab keeps no log apart from the page.
  - `cancelJob` aborts the job and appends the end `cancelled`.
- **`writtenAfterCancel`.** It is `[]`: MOD-runtimes' Uses gives no way to read a branch's commits.

No existing test's expected result changes. `runOnTab` keeping a job's abort changes nothing it returns or appends.

## Acceptance

- Against a fixture host and a fixture Bridge, each route gives the live state its record and the route report. The log
  is given as it grows, and the cancel ends the job with the end `cancelled`, after which nothing more is written.
- The first commit holds only the tests, and CI is red on it, the stub run recorded where only a missing export makes it
  red.
- Each test states its expected values in its own text.

# ITM-546 The host lists, follows and cancels CI runs

**REGISTER**

## Outcome

MOD-repository-hosts' `listCiRuns`, `cancelCiRun` and `ciRunLog`, as its file states them, on GitHub and on a GitLab
server. `src/repository-hosts/` names them only in comments, and the host `connect` returns has none of them. So
`fetchFailures` in `src/settings-pages/library.mjs` finds no failure, because it asks only a host that has both. ITM-535's
CI route finds no run either.

The readings, settled from the module file and from what `startWorkflow` already does in the two adapters:
- **Through a clone.** Each of the three uses the REST adapter where a token is given, and otherwise throws
  `NotSupported`, as `connect` states ("every other function uses the REST adapter where a token is given, or throws
  `NotSupported`") and as `startWorkflow` does in `src/repository-hosts/index.mjs`.
- **`listCiRuns(filter)` on GitHub.** "List workflow runs for a workflow" (`…/actions/workflows/{workflow}/runs`) where
  `workflow` is given, and "List workflow runs for a repository" (`…/actions/runs`) where it is not. `branch` and `commit`
  are sent as the server's `branch` and `head_sha`. The answers are read page by page with the adapter's `everyPage`.
  - Each run is a `CiRun`:
    - `id` is the run's id, as a string;
    - `workflow` is the workflow's file name, the last part of its `path`;
    - `commit` is `head_sha`, and `event` is `event`;
    - `url` is `html_url`, the address `startWorkflow` returns and MOD-workflow-entries writes as `by:`;
    - `started` is `run_started_at`, and `ended` is `updated_at` once the run is completed, otherwise `null`.
  - **`state`.**
    - `waiting` is `waiting`;
    - `in_progress` is `running`;
    - `queued`, `requested` and `pending` are `queued`;
    - a completed run takes its conclusion: `success`, `cancelled` and `skipped` as named, and every other conclusion
      `failure`.
- **`listCiRuns(filter)` on GitLab.** "List project pipelines", with `ref` and `sha` from `branch` and `commit`, read page
  by page. A GitLab project has one pipeline definition, which `startWorkflow` starts whatever workflow it is given. So
  `workflow` narrows nothing there, and each run's `workflow` is the filter's `workflow`, or `""` without one. The other
  fields are mapped as `startWorkflow` maps a pipeline, with the adapter's `STATES` table.
- **`cancelCiRun(id)`.** GitHub's "Cancel a workflow run" or GitLab's "Cancel a pipeline's jobs". A run that has already
  ended is not a failure: it returns, and the run's state shows that it ended ("the run's state shows when it has").
  Every other refusal goes through the adapter's existing refusal, as for `startWorkflow`.
- **`ciRunLog(id)`.** The texts of the run's jobs, in the order the server lists them, each preceded by a line with the
  job's name.
  - GitHub: "List jobs for a workflow run", then "Download job logs for a workflow run" for each job.
  - GitLab: "List pipeline jobs", then "Get a log file" for each job.
  - `null` where the server keeps no log of any of its jobs, that is, where every job's log is answered 404 or 410. A run
    the server does not know fails `NotFound`, as `readSnapshot` does.
  - This item does not establish whether GitHub's log redirect answers a page's `fetch` across origins. A `fetch` that
    throws fails `Unreachable`, as every call in the adapter does.

No existing test's expected result changes. The tests of `fetchFailures` and of ITM-535 use fixture hosts. Through the
real host, the library page now sends requests it did not send before. So the tests of `src/settings-pages/library.mjs`
and its callers are run under a `fetch` spy.

## Acceptance

- Against a fetch fixture for each server, `listCiRuns` gives the runs with the fields and states above, with and
  without `workflow`, `branch` and `commit`; `cancelCiRun` makes the one cancel request, and returns for a run that has
  already ended; `ciRunLog` gives the jobs' texts in order, and `null` where no job's log is kept.
- Each of the three names how it fails: `TokenRefused`, `PermissionMissing`, `RateLimited` and `Unreachable` as the file
  states, with a known positive beside each failure. Through a clone without a token, each throws `NotSupported`.
- The first commit holds only the tests, and CI is red on it.
- Each test states its expected values in its own text, and runs under a fetch spy that records every request.

# ITM-547 An entry reads its environment on GitLab CI

**REGISTER**

## Outcome

MOD-workflow-entries' `CiEnvironment`, as its file states it, for an entry run by the GitLab job workflow that
MOD-runtimes writes (`src/runtimes/workflow/gitlab.yml`). Today `ciEnvironment` in `src/workflow-entries/compose.mjs`
reads only GitHub Actions' variables, and its `service` is always `github`. On GitLab, `onDispatch` therefore finds no
input `job`.

The readings, settled from the module file, the GitLab template and GitLab's predefined variables (docs.gitlab.com,
"Predefined CI/CD variables"):
- **Which service.** It is `gitlab` where `GITLAB_CI` is `true`, and `github` otherwise, as today.
- **The event and the inputs.**
  - The event's `name` is `CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE`.
  - Its `payload` is `{ inputs }`, where `inputs` holds `job`, `task` and `endpoint` from `AGENT_M_INPUT_JOB`,
    `AGENT_M_INPUT_TASK` and `AGENT_M_INPUT_ENDPOINT`, which ITM-532's template sets. Each is held only where it is not
    empty. `onDispatch` reads `env.event.payload?.inputs` as it does on GitHub.
- **The checkouts and the repository.** The template runs the entry from `../instance`, a clone of the instance next to
  the product's checkout.
  - `checkout` is `CI_PROJECT_DIR`.
  - `repository` is `CI_PROJECT_URL`, and `branch` is `CI_COMMIT_REF_NAME`.
  - `agentM.commit` is `CI_COMMIT_SHA`, as `GITHUB_SHA` is on GitHub.
  - `job.productDir` is `AGENT_M_PRODUCT_DIR`, and `job.instanceDir` is `../instance` from `CI_PROJECT_DIR`.
- **The job's own fields.**
  - `job.actor` is `GITLAB_USER_LOGIN`.
  - `job.runUrl` is `CI_PIPELINE_URL`. This is the pipeline's `web_url`, which ITM-546's `listCiRuns` gives as a run's
    `url`, so ITM-535's lookup by `by:` finds the run.
  - `job.summaryFile` is `null`: GitLab has no step summary, and the answer stays in the job's log.
  - `token` is `null`: no instance workflow runs on GitLab.
- **Unchanged.** `job.runner`, `job.tokenName`, `job.personToken` and `job.keys` keep the names the template already
  sets: `AGENT_M_RUNNER`, `AGENT_M_TOKEN_NAME`, `AGENT_M_TOKEN` and `AGENT_M_KEY_NAMES`.
- **Left as they are.** The other entries that read a GitHub event's payload are not changed: for them, the payload on
  GitLab holds only `inputs`.

No existing test's expected result changes: without `GITLAB_CI`, every field is read as today.

## Acceptance

- `runEntry("onDispatch", env)` with a GitLab environment gives the entry the service `gitlab`, the event `api` with the
  inputs `job`, `task` and `endpoint`, and each field above. An empty input is absent.
- Without `GITLAB_CI`, a GitHub environment gives the same `CiEnvironment` as before.
- The first commit holds only the tests, and CI is red on it.
- Each test states its expected values in its own text.

# ITM-548 The job workflow is added to a product's .gitlab-ci.yml, every other line kept

**REGISTER**

## Outcome

On a GitLab product, the settings page installs Agent M's job workflow without replacing the product's own
`.gitlab-ci.yml`. Today `jobWorkflowFiles` returns a whole `.gitlab-ci.yml`: the `spec:` header, the inputs and the
include. Its one caller, `src/settings-pages/settings.mjs` (around line 714), commits that file whole. A product's own
pipeline is lost that way, against MOD-test-schedule's Data, which keeps every other line.

It builds on the draft of MOD-runtimes' `jobWorkflowFiles`, which is open for akmaier's acceptance (`docs/architecture/MOD-runtimes.md`,
Interfaces).
- **The new parameter.** `jobWorkflowFiles` takes `gitlabCi`, the product's `.gitlab-ci.yml` at the head that was read.
- **What it adds.** It returns that text with three things added, each only where it is missing:
  - the three inputs under `spec:`;
  - the entry under `include:`;
  - the inputs the entry passes on.

  Every other line stays as it is.
- **The caller.** The settings page passes the file it reads from the snapshot, as it already reads it to show whether
  the workflow is installed.

The draft was accepted with `220b55d0` (`docs/approvals/MOD-runtimes-7e3b846f59ed.md`).

The readings, settled at sprint team1/51's start:
- **The header.** Where the file has no `spec:` header, the header with the three inputs and its `---` are put before
  its first line. Where it has one, each of `job`, `task` and `endpoint` that is missing is added under its `inputs:`,
  with `default: ""`.
- **The include.** Where the file has `include:` as a list, the entry `- local: ".gitlab/agent-m-jobs.yml"` with its
  `inputs:` is added at the list's end, unless an entry names that file already. Where the file has no `include:`, the
  key and the entry are added at the end of the document.
- **A file it cannot add to safely.** Where `include:` holds a single string or a map, the change would rewrite a line
  of the product's own. `jobWorkflowFiles` then throws a `RuntimeError` named `GitlabCiNotList`, naming the file, and
  nothing is written. The settings page shows its message beside *Install*. "Every other line stays as it is" forbids
  the rewrite, so the refusal is the reading that keeps it.
- **An `inputs:` written inline.** This is settled at its first gate (#627, `c10480b7`). A `spec:` header's `inputs:`, or
  the existing entry's `inputs:`, written inline, such as `inputs: {}`, would also have to be rewritten to add to it.
  Adding a second `inputs:` block beside it would give the map the key twice. So it is refused with the same
  `GitlabCiNotList`, whose message names the part that is not written as a block. Nothing is written.
- **The caller.** `src/settings-pages/settings.mjs:822` passes the text of `.gitlab-ci.yml` read from the snapshot it
  already holds, `null` where there is none.
- **Existing tests.** None changes. `tests/runtimes-workflow.test.mjs` calls `jobWorkflowFiles` without `gitlabCi`, which
  gives the whole file as before. No settings test names `.gitlab-ci.yml`.

## Acceptance

- **A product without a `.gitlab-ci.yml`** gets the whole file, as ITM-532 writes it.
- **A product with its own `.gitlab-ci.yml`** keeps every line of it, and gains the header's inputs, the entry and its
  inputs where they are missing.
- **Installing again** changes nothing.
- **The settings page** commits the merged text.
- **The tests** state their expected text in their own text, and the first commit holds only them and is red.

# ITM-549 Where a text names a mail's people

**REGISTER**

## Outcome

MOD-personal-data's `personHits(text, people) -> Hit[]`, with the types `People` and `Hit`, as its file states them. It
is a pure function: no request, no file. `peopleIn`, which finds a mail's people, is ITM-550's.

The readings, settled from the module file ("every place in `text` where one of `people` appears: names also by their
parts, addresses also by their local part, phone numbers by their digits whatever the separators, regardless of case"):
- **A match** is case-insensitive and stands as a whole word. It is not a match where a letter or digit stands directly
  before or after it.
- **Names.** Each name is matched whole, and so is each of its parts. The parts are what blanks separate in the name,
  each kept as written, a period included.
- **Addresses.** Each address is matched whole, and so is its local part, the text before `@`.
- **Phone numbers.** In the text, a run of digits that may start with `+` and be separated by blanks, hyphens, slashes,
  dots or parentheses is a hit where its digits equal the digits of one of `people.phones`.
  - **Any stretch of the run counts.** A run may hold more than one number, such as a ticket number written before a
    phone number. So a stretch of whole digit groups within it is a hit where its digits equal the phone's digits. Such
    a stretch begins at the run's start or after a separator, and ends at the run's end or before a separator.
  - The item's text does not say "the longest run". Reading it so would add that word, and the phone number after other
    digits would go unfound (`A TEXT FROM A MAIL IS SEARCHED FOR THAT MAIL'S PEOPLE`).
- **Accounts.** Each account is matched as given, with or without a leading `@`.
- **A hit.**
  - `kind` is the kind of what was found, and `value` the text as it stands in `text`.
  - `line` and `column` count from 1, where the hit begins.
  - Where a part of a name and the whole name are both found at the same place, the whole name is the hit.
- **The order.** Hits are given by line, then column. An empty list means the text names none of them.

No existing test's expected result changes.

## Acceptance

- **Each kind is found.** A planted name, one of its parts, an address, its local part, a phone number written with
  other separators, and an account with and without `@` are each found with their kind, value, line and column.
- **Counter-proofs.** A text without any of them gives `[]`. A word that only contains a name part, such as "Annabel"
  for "Anna", is no hit.
- **Tests first.** The first commit holds only the tests, and CI is red on it. No stub is committed.
- **Expected values in the tests.** Each test states its expected values in its own text.

# ITM-565 TST-276005 times out in CI

**REGISTER**

## Outcome

TST-276005 (`tests/desktop-shell.test.mjs`, "native close behavior and a second source start restore the first window")
timed out after 120 seconds in CI, then passed on a re-run, in a pull request that touched neither the desktop shell nor
its tests. ITM-541 and ITM-557 made its Openbox install wait for a slow mirror and for the package lock. This is a new
mode: the test itself ran out of time.

**The failing log.** The Scrum Master's copy of job 117132128493's log was fetched at 18:35 UTC, before the re-run. The
logs endpoint now gives the second attempt's content for that id. The copy shows:
- `not ok 92 - TST-276005` (line 777), finished at 18:34:28.97, with `failureType: 'testTimeoutFailure'` and `test timed
  out after 120000ms` (lines 782–783);
- `The operation was canceled.` at 18:34:44.93 (line 786).

So the test itself ran out of its 120 seconds, not the Openbox install.

**Where the 120 seconds went**, read by the Scrum Master from that copy:
- **Not the install.** The Openbox install ended at 18:32:24.11 (status 0), and the fixture was ready at 18:32:24.12.
- **The other tests were quick.** TST-276001–004 and TST-276006 passed in about a second each.
- **TST-276005 stalled.** Its probes ran at 18:32:28.98, 18:32:29.60 and 18:32:30.02–30.03, the last being the second
  start's probe. Then the log holds nothing for 118.9 seconds, until `not ok 92` at 18:34:28.97.

**Why a wait can take minutes and say nothing**, read from `tests/desktop-shell.test.mjs`:
- `wait` (line 26) tries its condition 240 times, 125 ms apart, and swallows every error (`catch {}`). It ends with
  "Timed out waiting for real Electron." and does not say what it waited for.
- Each try is an `evaluate` through `cdp` (lines 160–173), which allows up to 5 seconds to open the socket and 5 more for
  the answer.
- So a main process that stops answering makes each try take up to 10 seconds. The intended bound of about 30 seconds
  becomes up to 40 minutes, and the test's own 120 seconds end it first, with nothing printed.

After the second start, the test waits in turn for:
- `__agentMSecondInstanceCount === count + 1`;
- the second start's exit (`within`, 5 seconds, named);
- the first window visible and not minimised.

One of these never held, and the log cannot say which.

**The settled measure.** It finds where the time goes; it is not a skip:
- **`wait` gets a deadline in time.** It allows 30 seconds from its start, whatever each try takes.
- **It names what it waited for.** It takes a name for its condition. On the deadline it throws "<name> did not hold
  within 30 s", with the last error a try threw.
- **Each wait in TST-276005 gets its name.** For example, "the first window counts the second start", or "the first
  window is visible and not minimised again".
- **One helper.** `tests/release-itm-276-desktop-shell.test.mjs` (line 31) holds the same `wait`, so the helper moves into
  one file both import, `tests/desktop-shell.d/wait.mjs`, whose header names MOD-desktop-shell (AGENTS.md §2, "Nothing
  twice").

The next time the test fails in CI, its message then names the condition that did not hold. If the product itself never
restores the window, that becomes a finding of MOD-desktop-shell for an item of its own.

**Existing tests.** No expected result changes; only the helper's bound and message change. The release test's file
changes, so its developer implements none of MOD-desktop-shell and records its local run before and after.

## Acceptance

- **The bound holds.** A planted condition that never holds makes `wait` throw within 30 seconds, naming the condition
  and the last error. Its message is checked by a test of the helper.
- **The test is unchanged.** TST-276005 passes as before, with every expected value unchanged.
- **The release test.** TST-276901's file passes before and after, and its run is recorded.

# ITM-572 The prompt bar prepares a hand-over of every kind on every page

**REGISTER**

## Outcome

The prompt bar prepares a hand-over in the tab (`prepareJob` in `src/prompt-bar/hand-over.mjs`) before `handOverJob`
queues it. The tab holds only the strategies that the page's views hand `start.mjs`, as ARC-038 has it ("The entry
pages register the strategies of the modules the views include"). So a hand-over of `implement` from a page whose views
do not include its recipes and preconditions is refused with `UnknownStrategy` at the click, even once ITM-568 builds
`implementation-inputs`. Its recipes are `implementation-inputs`, `chapters-for-implementation` and `instruction?`, and
its precondition is `rests-on-accepted`.

Two facts bind the design:
- MOD-job-runner refuses a strategy registered twice (`DuplicateStrategy`, `src/job-runner/registry.mjs:18`).
- MOD-implementation-pages' view is to hand `runStrategies` too.

**The design was accepted by akmaier** in `3aff8ad9` (ARC-038, MOD-prompt-bar, MOD-site-frame), and each decision names
the principle it rests on:
- **One responsibility.** The frame registers every strategy set in the tab, in `start.mjs`, as ARC-038 has the entry
  pages do. A view or the bar only names the sets its kinds need.
- **No special first case.** The bar names its sets the way a view does: MOD-prompt-bar's new `handOverStrategies`. These
  are the sets the job workflow registers in CI, since a handed-over job runs on CI or on a Bridge.
- **Nothing twice.** Each set is registered once per tab, however many views or the bar hand it. The accepted texts
  already have several views on the review page hand the same set (`approvalStrategies` from MOD-review-pages,
  MOD-implementation-pages and MOD-test-pages). Registered once per view, that throws `DuplicateStrategy`
  (`src/job-runner/registry.mjs:18`).
- **Adding one of a kind changes nothing of another kind.** A new view, or a new set a view hands, changes neither the
  frame nor the bar.

The lists of CI (MOD-workflow-entries) and of the Bridge (MOD-desktop-shell) name the same thirteen sets that
`handOverStrategies` names. Making them one list is not part of this item.

**The readings, settled at sprint team1/54:**
- **Which sets `handOverStrategies` holds.** Of the thirteen its file names, the sets that are built and exported today:
  - `approvalStrategies`, `specStrategies`, `editStrategies`;
  - `sourceStrategies`, `reuseStrategies`, `resourceStrategies`;
  - `runStrategies`.

  The others (`workStrategies`, `processStrategies`, `scheduleStrategies`, `resultStrategies`, `issueStrategies`,
  `routeStrategies`) join as the items that build them add them. `git grep -E "export const [a-zA-Z]+Strategies" -- src`
  lists the seven.
- **Registering each set once.**
  - `start.mjs` registers the views' sets and then `handOverStrategies`, the bar's under the owner `MOD-prompt-bar`, and
    skips a set object it has already registered on that load.
  - In a tab, `start.mjs` runs once. TST-531013 evaluates it a second time in the same process and expects the load not
    to reject. So a `DuplicateStrategy` whose first owner is the owner now registering (`error.owners[0]`) is a set
    already registered and is skipped. Any other `DuplicateStrategy` still throws.
- **Which hand-overs prepare.**
  - Every kind whose preconditions, recipes, checks, steps and writer are all among the handed sets and the runner's
    built-ins prepares without `UnknownStrategy`. Among them are the change kinds.
  - `implement` still meets `UnknownStrategy` for its writer `branch-and-pull-request` until ITM-567 builds
    `routeStrategies` and ITM-605 hands it. `prepareJob` names the writer among the strategies it checks
    (`src/job-runner/prepare.mjs:25-31`).
- **Existing tests.** The tests were grepped for `site-frame/start.mjs` and `DuplicateStrategy`.
  - TST-531012's fixture views share no set with the bar, so its owners hold.
  - TST-531013 holds by the second reading above.
  - `tests/system-uc-019-change-requirements-by-prompt.test.mjs:154` composes the views' sets itself and imports no
    `start.mjs`, so it holds.

## Acceptance

- On the main page and on the review pages, a hand-over of each kind whose strategies are all handed is prepared
  without `UnknownStrategy`.
- No strategy set is registered twice.
- The first commit holds only the tests, and CI is red on it. No stub is committed.

# ITM-603 Leaving an edit route with unsaved changes asks first

**REGISTER**

## Outcome

UC-018 7a: "The dashboard asks before discarding them". MOD-markdown-render's `Editor.close()` asks (TST-343005), but no route calls it when the address changes.

**Who calls `close()` on a route change, read at sprint team1/56.** No text says.
- MOD-markdown-render's editor "asks first" when it is left, and `close()` asks (`src/markdown-render/editor.mjs:106`).
- The frame shows the next route on every `hashchange` (`src/site-frame/index.mjs:283`), so the route is replaced before
  anything could ask. A `hashchange` cannot be cancelled once it has happened.

So the frame has to ask the route shown before it shows another one. That needs a draft, committed on `main` for
akmaier:
- **MOD-site-frame.** `Route` gains `leave?: () -> boolean`. Before the frame shows another route on a change of the
  address, it asks the route shown, and `false` keeps that route and puts its address back.
- **MOD-markdown-render.** `Editor.close() -> boolean` asks first when the text holds unsaved changes, and says whether
  the editor closed.
- **MOD-review-pages.** The edit routes' `leave` closes their editor through `close`.

Each decision names its principle:
- *One responsibility:* the frame routes, the route knows its editor, and the editor knows its unsaved text.
- *No special first case:* `leave` is optional for every route, as `subject` is.

**Existing tests.** `tests/markdown-render-343.test.mjs:119-148` calls `close()` and ignores what it returns, so it
holds. No frame test asserts a route's replacement against a `leave`.

**Ready to be selected** once akmaier accepts the draft.

**Settled at sprint team1/69's start. Selectable.**
- **The modules whose files it changes:**
  - MOD-site-frame: `index.mjs`. Before it shows another route on a `hashchange` (`:305` for the review and main
    pages), it asks the route shown through its optional `leave()`. `false` keeps the route and puts its address back.
  - MOD-markdown-render: `editor.mjs:105`, where `close()` returns whether the editor closed, and asks first when the
    text holds unsaved changes.
  - MOD-review-pages: its edit routes give `leave` that calls their editor's `close`.
  - All three texts are accepted (`b43da779`). No topic is added.
- **The grep, full output read:**
  - `grep -n hashchange src/site-frame/index.mjs` finds :305 and :370. :370 is the Bridge's window, whose routes have no
    editor. It gets the same call, since `leave` is optional for every route (no special first case).
  - `grep -n "close()" src/markdown-render/editor.mjs src/review-pages/*.mjs` finds the editor's definition alone, so no
    route calls `close` today.

# ITM-611 A section edit's fallback pages say which file changed since the edit began

**REGISTER**

## Outcome

Without a token, `proposeSection` and `saveEntry` return `fallbackEditLinks` for the entry's files. Each file's
`existing` is taken from the snapshot read at the save (`src/spec-changes/propose.mjs:386-388` and `:422-424`), which is
also the snapshot `fallbackEditLinks` compares against. So `differs` is always false, and UC-018 4a's "warns if one
already differs" never shows.

`existing` is to say whether the file existed when the edit began, as MOD-artifact-edits defines `differs`: "the file on
the default branch is no longer what the edit started from".

**The design, a draft for akmaier on `main`** (MOD-spec-changes, Interfaces, `proposeSection` and `saveEntry`).
- **What changes.** Both functions take `openedHead`, the commit the edit was opened on. A fallback page's `differs` says
  whether its file exists on the default branch otherwise than at `openedHead`.
- **The principles it rests on.**
  - *One responsibility.* The writer that builds the pages also knows where the edit began, so the caller passes that
    in and computes nothing.
  - *Nothing twice.* `fallbackEditLinks` keeps its definition of `differs` (MOD-artifact-edits). Only the input it is
    given changes.
  - *No special first case.* `openedHead` stands beside `openedBlob`, which already says what the edit started from.
- **The callers.** All in MOD-review-pages, each holding the snapshot it opened on, whose `commit` it passes:
  - `src/review-pages/edit.mjs:92`;
  - `src/review-pages/requirements-draft.mjs:73`;
  - `src/review-pages/entry-edit.mjs:71`.
- **Existing tests.**
  - Every test that calls the two functions gains `openedHead` in its input:
    - `tests/spec-changes-propose-section.test.mjs`, where TST-472992 asserts `differs` false at `:273`;
    - `tests/spec-changes-save-entry.test.mjs` (`:176`).

- **Ready to be selected** once akmaier accepts the draft.

**Settled at sprint team1/71's start. Selectable.**

# ITM-626 A hand-over gives each kind the parameters its strategies read

The bar's hand-over names what it works on in the job's parameters through `paramsOf` (`src/prompt-bar/hand-over.mjs:89`).
For `works_on: ["UC-007"]` that gives `{ useCases: ["UC-007"] }`. `queue()` prepares `change-use-case` with it.

That kind's recipe `use-case-with-neighbours` reads "the use case named in the job's parameters" (MOD-approvals) as

record is written and the hand-over reaches the workflow's dispatch.

- **The keys come from the strategies, not from the bar.**
  - The parameter keys are the ones the kind's strategies read, as the pages that start the same kind pass them.
  - The bar gives each key that `works_on` determines:
    - `useCase` for a single use case, beside `useCases`;
    - `requirements`, `useCases`, `items`, and `steps` for plan steps.
  - It invents none.
- **Every handed kind is checked, not only `change-use-case`.**
  - Before the code, the developer lists, for every kind whose strategies `handOverStrategies` holds, the `params.*` its
    strategies read. A grep of the strategies' files finds, among others:
    - `useCase`;
    - `requirements` and `useCases` (`rests-on-accepted`);
    - `items` and `steps`;
    - `source`, `resource`, `kind`, `entry` and `part`.
  - Keys that `works_on` cannot give, such as a source, a resource, or a group's kind, are not invented. Such a kind
    keeps failing its preparation in the tab with the strategy's own error, by name, and nothing is queued.
- **Existing tests.** `tests/prompt-bar-hand-over.test.mjs` asserts no parameters of a record. A grep of the file for
  `params` finds none, while `works_on` is found 5 times as the known positive.
- **Reachable through the real host.** The hand-over is prepared in the tab and queued on CI or a Bridge, which the
  developer reached up to the dispatch.

## Acceptance

- A hand-over of `change-use-case` on one use case is prepared and queued, its record carrying `useCase`.
- For every handed kind, the test states which of its parameters a hand-over gives and which it cannot. A kind whose

  (`b43da779`). The view classifies nothing itself, as the cut from ITM-597 asks.
- **The grep, full output read:** `grep -rn "Open proposals\|queues(\|entryView" src/trace-pages tests` finds three
  tests whose expected results change:

  - `:602-611` (TST-597015): no section, no stale note and no queue read;

  - ITM-597's first draft measured the queues' files at 110 raw reads without a token, with a token batched.
  - **The measurement asked** (sprint 67): a committed test counting the snapshot's reads on a fixture with two open
    entries. It shows one `queues` read per version, one `entryView` per open entry, and none on reopening.

- **Sprint 68:** no release test is among the tests it is known to change. If the draft run finds one, the developer stops
