# MOD-text-tools The text primitives every format uses

## Responsibility

It belongs to the artifact model (ARC-048). It offers the primitives every format of the review layout is built on:
front matter, the two hashes Agent M names texts by, line differences, the one form of a finding, and the marks of
history a document must not carry. It runs unchanged in a browser and in Node; it keeps no state and performs no input
or output.

## Parts

- `index.mjs` — the interface.
- `front-matter.mjs` — reading and writing front matter.
- `hashes.mjs` — git's blob SHA-1 and SHA-256, through the platform's WebCrypto.
- `line-diff.mjs` — the line difference of two texts.
- `findings.mjs` — the finding, its text form, and reading it back.
- `history-marks.mjs` — the marks of history in a document.

## Data

It keeps nothing. It owns two formats.

**Front matter.** A text begins with a line `---`, then lines of keys, then a line `---`; the body is every byte after the
closing line. Lines end in LF or in CR LF, and a value never keeps its CR. A key is `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*`, followed by `:`.
A key with a value on its line holds that value as text, trimmed; a key with nothing after its colon, or with `[]`,
holds a list, whose items are the following lines of the form `  - item`. There is no nesting, no quoting and no other
syntax; a text without the opening line has no front matter, and all of it is body.

```text
---
id: MOD-text-tools
follows:
  - ARC-048
uses:
---
# MOD-text-tools …
```

**The finding**, in the one form `A FINDING READS LIKE A COMPILER MESSAGE` demands — as data, and as one line of text:

```text
{ artifact: "UC-007", line: 12, kind: "error", rule: "A USE CASE REALISES NAMED REQUIREMENTS",
  what: "realises \"EXPORT AS PDF\" matches no requirement", fix: "use an existing name or remove the line" }

UC-007:12: error: realises "EXPORT AS PDF" matches no requirement [A USE CASE REALISES NAMED REQUIREMENTS] — use an existing name or remove the line.
```

`artifact` is the identifier of the artifact the finding concerns — or, for a file without an identifier, its path;
`line` counts from 1 in that artifact's file; `kind` is `error` or `warning`; `rule` is a requirement's name exactly as
the SPEC writes it; `what` says what is wrong; `fix` says the correction expected.

## Interfaces

- `FrontMatter` — `{ fields: Record<string, string | string[]>, order: string[], body: string, bodyLine: number }`: the
  fields by key, the keys in the order they stand, the body, and the line on which the body begins (from 1).
- `Finding` — `{ artifact: string, line: number, kind: "error" | "warning", rule: string, what: string, fix: string }`, as
  defined under Data.
- `DiffLine` — `{ op: "same" | "added" | "removed", text: string, before: number | null, after: number | null }`: one
  line of a difference, with its line in the text before and in the text after, where it has one.
- `HistoryMark` — `{ line: number, kind: "withdrawal" | "edit-stamp" | "dated-change", text: string }`: one place in a
  document that records history (`A DOCUMENT HOLDS NO HISTORY`).
- `parseFrontMatter(text: string) -> FrontMatter` — reads the front matter of a text as defined under Data. It never
  throws: a text without front matter, or whose closing line is missing, has empty `fields` and is all body. A caller
  that requires front matter checks that `order` is not empty.
- `formatFrontMatter(fields: Record<string, string | string[]>, order: string[], body: string) -> string` — writes front
  matter with the keys in `order`, each list one item per line and an empty list as `key:` alone, then the body
  unchanged; `formatFrontMatter` of what `parseFrontMatter` read gives back the same bytes for a text written in this
  form. Throws `TypeError` for a key that is not `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*`, or a value holding a line break.
- `blobSha(text: string) -> Promise<string>` — git's blob SHA-1 of the text's UTF-8 bytes: 40 lowercase hexadecimal
  digits, the same as `git hash-object` gives for the file. The text is hashed as given; a caller that read a file must
  pass its exact bytes, line endings included, or the SHA names another text.
- `sha256(content: string | Uint8Array) -> Promise<string>` — the SHA-256 of the bytes, or of a string's UTF-8 bytes, as
  64 lowercase hexadecimal digits.
- `lineDiff(before: string, after: string) -> DiffLine[]` — the lines of two texts as a difference: every line of both,
  in order, each `same`, `added` or `removed`, with as few `added` and `removed` lines as the two texts allow. Line
  endings are not part of a line, so a text that changed only its line endings shows no difference; a caller that must
  know whether two texts are byte-identical compares their `blobSha`.
- `finding(fields: Finding) -> Finding` — a finding, checked: throws `TypeError` when `kind` is neither `error` nor
  `warning`, when `line` is not a whole number of at least 1, or when `rule` is not a requirement's name in capitals.
  Every module that reports a finding makes it with this function.
- `formatFinding(finding: Finding) -> string` — the finding as its one line of text, as defined under Data.
- `parseFinding(line: string) -> Finding | null` — a line of that form read back; `null` for any other line.
- `historyMarks(text: string) -> HistoryMark[]` — the places of a document that record its history, each told by its
  words: a note that something was withdrawn (`withdrawal`); a stamp of who edited what or when, such as
  `Last edited by …` or `reworded <date>` (`edit-stamp`); and a date given as the date of a change (`dated-change`) —
  after a word of decision or acceptance, `PO decision <date>`, or set off by a comma as the date of an attribution,
  `(PO A. Maier, <date>)` or `PO, <date>: …`. Any other date is no mark: a document states the dates its content needs —
  the date a fact was read (`DUE DILIGENCE IS FETCHED, NOT RECALLED`), a version, a release, a measurement it names —,
  with the words that say what they are or in a table's cells. So every mark is history: a caller whose kind of document
  must hold none reports each one, without telling dates apart itself; records and measurements are dated by nature, and
  their callers do not ask.

## Files

It reads and writes no file.

## Uses

It uses no other module. The hashes use the WebCrypto interface that browsers and Node both offer.

# MOD-trace-graph The trace graph and everything derived from it

## Responsibility

It belongs to the artifact model (ARC-048). From the files of one repository at one commit it builds the graph of every
identifier and of what names it — requirements, use cases, architecture decisions, modules, tests, items, the sources a
requirement names, and the code files in the modules' folders —, and derives from that graph alone what needs several
artifacts at once: the checks across artifacts, the traces of a requirement, the coverage gaps, the impact lists of a
change, the order of the modules by their uses, the module rows of UC-025, the comparison of two versions, and
references to what exists only inside Agent M. The matrix is derived from the files of one commit alone and edited by no one (`THE TRACEABILITY
MATRIX IS DERIVED`): `traceGraph` builds it, and where the repository holds the graph of that very commit on its branch
`trace-cache`, `traceGraph` returns that graph and reads no file. It runs in a browser and in Node; it reads only through the
source it is given and writes only through `publishGraph`, which adds the graph of one commit to that branch.

## Parts

- `index.mjs` — the interface.
- `build.mjs` — reading the artifacts of a repository into the graph, with the facts its checks need.
- `code.mjs` — code files by module folder, and the imports between module folders.
- `checks.mjs` — the checks across artifacts.
- `derive.mjs` — traces, gaps, impact lists, module order and rows, comparison.
- `stored.mjs` — the graph of one commit as a text and back, and adding it to the branch `trace-cache`.
- **Taken over, outside this folder** (`CODE OUTSIDE THE ARCHITECTURE IS MOVED INTO IT`; the count in `docs/measurements/2026-10-17_code-outside-every-module.md`). Each file goes as stated, in this module's own implementation jobs:
  - `docs/assets/traceability.mjs`, `docs/assets/traceability/graph.mjs`: removed once this module gives `moduleRows` and no file imports them. `tests/architecture-format.test.mjs`, a file the module MOD-documents takes over, imports `moduleHeaders` from the first; no interface of this module gives the `Module:` header lines of code files, so that import and the test of `moduleHeaders` go in MOD-documents' job, before these two files are removed.
  - `tests/test_coverage_report.py`: rewritten on `traceGraph` and `graphFindings`: it is the Check of `EVERY CODE FILE BELONGS TO A MODULE`. Its half on tests and test helpers that name no module stays as it reads them now, since no interface of this module gives a test file's `Module:` header.
  - `tests/test_impact_list.py`, `tests/test_matrix_derived.py`, `tests/test_references.py`, `tests/release-sprint-02-d-traceability.test.mjs`: rewritten on this module, or removed with the old graph.

## Data

It keeps nothing between calls. A graph lives as long as its caller holds it, or on the branch `trace-cache` of the repository,
which only grows: the file `<commit>.json` is the text `graphText` gives for the graph of the commit it is named by, the
file `<commit>.impacts.json` holds the impact lists of that commit's decision and module files that are not accepted, and no
file of it is changed or deleted.

What it reads, and as what:

| Path | Read as |
|---|---|
| `SPEC.md` | requirements, through MOD-spec-document |
| `docs/use-cases/UC-*.md`, `docs/architecture/ARC-*.md`, `docs/architecture/MOD-*.md`, `docs/plan/ITM-*.md`, `docs/backlog/ITM-*.md` | documents, through MOD-documents with the schemas it owns |
| test files, as MOD-test-document's `isTestFile` tells them | test declarations, through MOD-test-document |
| `docs/groups/<kind>.md` | the groups' titles, through MOD-group-document, so that a group's title named where an identifier is expected is found |
| code files — files whose extension is one of those listed below, outside `docs/`, test files and folders named `vendor` or `node_modules` | paths, and for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python and CSS the modules they import |

A code file belongs to the module whose `folder` holds it; a module's folder is named after its identifier (`A MODULE IS
A FOLDER`). The graph holds no field for it: a code node's module is the module whose `folder` is the beginning of its
path, and a code file in no module's folder belongs to none.

The extensions of the four languages whose imports are read, and what an import is in each:

| Language | Extensions | An import is |
|---|---|---|
| JavaScript | `js`, `mjs`, `cjs`, `jsx` | a static `import … from "x"`, `import "x"` or `export … from "x"`, a `import("x")` and a `require("x")` whose argument is a string literal |
| TypeScript | `ts`, `tsx`, `mts`, `cts` | as in JavaScript |
| Python | `py` | `import a.b` and `from a.b import c`, where the dotted name is a path from the repository's root, and `from . import c` or `from ..a import c`, relative to the file's directory |
| CSS | `css` | `@import "x"` and `@import url("x")` |

The other extensions of code files, whose imports are not read: `rb`, `go`, `rs`, `java`, `kt`, `kts`, `scala`, `c`, `h`,
`cc`, `cpp`, `hpp`, `cs`, `swift`, `m`, `php`, `pl`, `lua`, `r`, `jl`, `sh`, `bash`, `zsh`, `ps1`, `sql`, `scss`, `html`,
`vue`, `svelte`, `dart`, `ex`, `exs`, `erl`, `hs`, `ml`, `fs`, `clj`.

A specifier that begins with `.` is resolved against the importing file's directory, any other against the repository's
root. The module imported is the one whose `folder` is the beginning of the resolved path. An `imports` edge is made only
when that module is another than the importing file's own; a specifier that names no path of the repository (a package, a
`node:` name) and a path in no module's folder make none.

The graph keeps, while it is built, every fact a check across artifacts needs, so that each check is decided from the
graph alone and no file is read twice:

- a node keeps from its file what the checks read: a module its `folder` and the interfaces it `provides`, a plan step or
  backlog item its `level` and its `tests`, a requirement the items of its source as written;
- a `uses` edge keeps the interface it names after the module, such as `parseSpec` in `MOD-spec-document.parseSpec`;
- a group's title is a node of the kind `group`, keyed by its file and line, since a group carries no identifier (`A
  GROUP CARRIES NO IDENTIFIER`);
- the graph keeps the path of every file of the repository, each link an artifact writes — a Markdown link
  `[text](target)` or an autolink `<target>` — with its target as written, and the references by position that
  MOD-identifiers' `positionalReferences` finds in each artifact's text.

The sources a requirement names are kept on its node, not as links: no file the graph reads names a source by an
identifier, and which register entry an item names is MOD-source-register's to say.

## Interfaces

- `TextSource` — `{ paths: string[], read(path: string) -> Promise<string | null>, readMany?: (paths: string[]) ->
  Promise<void>, readOn?: (branch: string, path: string) -> Promise<string | null> }`: the files of one repository at one commit, as the caller hands them; a snapshot of Access fits it.
  `readMany`, where the source offers it, is told every path the graph will read before the first `read`, so that a
  source on a server reads them in batches. `readOn`, where the source offers it, reads a file of another branch of the
  same repository, as a snapshot of Access does; a source without it, such as one that holds an edited text in place of a
  file, never uses a stored graph.
- `Graph` — `{ commit: string | null, nodes: Map<string, { id: string, kind: IdentifierKind | "code" | "group", path:
  string, line: number, title: string | null, blob: string | null, folder: string | null, provides: string[] | null,
  level: string | null, tests: string[] | null, sources: string[] | null }>, edges: { from: string, to: string, via:
  "realises" | "forced_by" | "designs" | "follows" | "refines" | "uses" | "guards" | "exercises" | "changes" | "builds_on" |
  "imports" | "names", interface: string | null, path: string, line: number }[], files: string[], links: { from: string,
  target: string, path: string, line: number }[], positions: Finding[], unread: { path: string, reason: string }[] }` —
  every node and every link, with the facts listed under Data: a node's field that its kind does not have is `null`, and a
  group's node is keyed `<path>:<line>`; an edge's `interface` is `null` but for `uses`; `files` every path the
  `TextSource` lists; `links` each link an artifact writes, `from` the artifact's identifier; `positions` the warnings of
  `positionalReferences`, as it gives them; `unread` the files it could not read, with the reason; a code
  node's `id` is its path, its `line` is 1 and its `title`, `blob` and other facts are `null`; an `imports` edge's `from` is
  the importing code node's `id`, its `to` the identifier of the module imported, its `path` and `line` the file and line of
  the import. A code file of another extension is a node and is not read, so `readMany` is not told it; that its imports
  are not read follows from its extension, as `moduleRows`' `importsRead` says.
- `Traces` — `{ sources: string[], useCases: string[], decisions: string[], modules: string[], tests: string[], items:
  string[] }`.
- `Gaps` — `{ requirementsWithoutUseCase: string[], requirementsWithoutModule: string[], requirementsWithoutTest:
  string[], useCasesWithoutRequirement: string[], unknownNames: { name: string, namedBy: { id: string, path: string,
  line: number }[] }[] }`.
- `ImpactEntry` — `{ id: string, kind: IdentifierKind, path: string, line: number, via: string }`: one artifact that names
  what changes, and how.
- `ArchitectureImpact` — `{ modules: { id: string, why: "changed" | "uses an interface that changes" | "uses an interface
  that is removed", breaks: boolean }[], codeFiles: string[], tests: { id: string, guards: string[] }[], named: { added:
  string[], removed: string[] }, items: string[] }`.
- `ModuleRow` — `{ module: string, subsystem: string | null, realises: string[], describedBy: string, code: string[],
  tests: string[], imports: string[], importsRead: boolean }`.
- `ModuleGap` — `{ kind: string, artifact: string, path: string, what: string }`, its `kind` one of the gaps
  `moduleRows` lists.
- `Comparison` — `{ requirements: { added: string[], changed: string[], removed: string[] }, coverage: { gained: { name:
  string, by: string }[], lost: { name: string, by: string }[] } }`.
- `traceGraph(source: TextSource, options?: { commit?: string }) -> Promise<Graph>` — first, where `options.commit` is
  given and the source has `readOn`, reads `<commit>.json` on the branch `trace-cache` once; a text that `graphFromText`
  restores for that commit is the result, and no file is read. A missing branch or file, a text of another format and a
  text that names another commit are not failures: the graph is then built as follows. Names to the source's `readMany`,
  where it has one, every file it will read, then reads the repository's artifacts and
  code files as listed under Data and builds the graph, keeping the facts listed there. A file that cannot be read, or not
  read as its format, is listed
  in `unread` with the reason, never left out silently; the findings of a single document's format are MOD-documents' and
  are not repeated here. Rejects only when `source.read` itself rejects, with that error.
- `graphFindings(graph: Graph) -> Finding[]` — the checks across artifacts, each decided from the graph alone and each an
  error naming the artifact and line:
  a name in `realises`, `forced_by`, an item's `realises` or a test's `guards` that matches no requirement or use case
  (`A USE CASE REALISES NAMED REQUIREMENTS`, `EVERY ARTIFACT NAMES ITS ORIGIN`); a `uses` edge whose interface the used
  module's node does not provide (`DEVELOP AGAINST INTERFACES`); a cycle among the modules' uses (`MODULES DEPEND ON EACH OTHER WITHOUT A CYCLE`);
  a module designed by no decision or by more than one, or that does not follow the decision that designs it (`A MODULE
  BELONGS TO ONE SUBSYSTEM`); more or fewer than one decision without `refines`, or a decision that does not refine it
  (`ONE DECISION STATES THE WHOLE ARCHITECTURE`); an item that names a module the architecture does not describe (`A
  BACKLOG ITEM NAMES THE MODULES IT CHANGES`), or a plan step whose `tests` are not those of its `level` (`A PLAN STEP
  NAMES THE TESTS OF ITS LEVEL`); a module whose `folder` is not named after its identifier, or lies inside another
  module's folder (`A MODULE IS A FOLDER`); a name where an identifier is expected that is the title of a `group` node (`A
  GROUP CARRIES NO IDENTIFIER`); a code file's `imports` edge to a module of which the file's own module names no
  interface among its `uses`, named at the file and line of the import with the module imported (`A MODULE STATES ITS
  RESPONSIBILITY AND ITS INTERFACES`), the same imports `moduleRows` lists as a gap; and, as the warnings they are, the
  graph's `positions` (`A REFERENCE NAMES THE IDENTIFIER, NOT THE POSITION`).
- `tracesTo(graph: Graph, name: string) -> Traces` — for a requirement, the items of its source its node keeps, and every
  use case, decision, module, test and item that names it (`A REQUIREMENT SHOWS WHAT TRACES TO IT`); a module traces to a
  requirement through the tests of it that guard the requirement.
- `coverageGaps(graph: Graph) -> Gaps` — the requirements no use case realises and — once modules and tests exist — no
  module realises and no test guards; the use cases that realise nothing; every name that matches no requirement, with
  what names it (`UNREALISED REQUIREMENTS ARE REPORTED, NOT FORBIDDEN`). The gaps are shown; none blocks anything.
- `requirementImpact(graph: Graph, name: string) -> ImpactEntry[]` — every artifact that names the requirement, which a
  change to it must list (`A REQUIREMENT IS NOT CHANGED WITHOUT AN IMPACT LIST`).
- `architectureImpact(graph: Graph, changes: { path: string, before: string | null, after: string | null }[]) ->
  ArchitectureImpact` — for changed, added or removed decision and module files: the modules they concern and the modules
  that use an interface they alter or remove, marked as breaking; the code files in each affected module's folder; the
  tests that exercise those modules and the requirements those tests guard; the requirements and use cases the files name
  and no longer name; the plan steps and backlog items that name an affected module (`AN ARCHITECTURE CHANGE IS NOT
  ACCEPTED WITHOUT AN IMPACT LIST`).
- `graphText(graph: Graph) -> string` — the graph as one text, the same text for the same graph, that names the commit the
  graph was built for.
- `graphFromText(text: string, commit: string) -> Graph | null` — the graph the text holds, or `null` for a text that is
  no `graphText` or names a commit other than `commit`. Reads nothing.
- `publishGraph(host: Host, snapshot: Snapshot, changed?: Array<{ path: string, before: { commit: string, text: string }
  | null }>) -> Promise<{ commit: string, written: boolean }>` — builds the graph of the snapshot's commit from its files
  and adds `<commit>.json` to the branch `trace-cache` by `commitFiles`, on the head it read; `written` is `false` when
  the branch holds the file already, which it then leaves as it is. With `changed`, the decision and module files of the
  commit that are not accepted, each with the text it was last accepted at and that text's commit (`null` for a file never
  accepted), as the caller reads them, it adds `<commit>.impacts.json` in the same commit: for each file, its path, its
  blob at the commit, `before`'s commit, and `architectureImpact(graph, [{ path, before: before.text, after }])`. This
  module reads no history and no approval record, so the caller hands `changed` in. Crosses the network; fails as
  `commitFiles` fails, with `NotFound` naming the branch when the repository has none.
- `storedImpacts(source: TextSource, commit: string) -> Promise<Map<string, { blob: string, before: string | null,
  impact: ArchitectureImpact }> | null>` — the impact lists stored for `commit` by `publishGraph`, keyed by path, read
  with the source's `readOn` in one request; `null` without `readOn`, or when the branch or the file is missing or holds
  another format. A caller uses an entry only while the file's blob is the one stored.
- `systemDecisions(graph: Graph) -> { system: string[], subsystems: string[] }` — the decisions that refine no other,
  and the subsystems' decisions: those that refine one of them and design at least one module; each list by identifier.
- `moduleOrder(graph: Graph) -> { order: string[] } | { cycle: string[] }` — the modules in an order in which every module
  stands after every module whose interfaces it uses, or the modules of a cycle when there is one (`A RUN FOLLOWS THE
  MODULES' INTERFACES`).
- `moduleRows(graph: Graph) -> { rows: ModuleRow[], gaps: ModuleGap[] }` — one row per module, as UC-025 shows it, and
  the gaps (`MODULE GAPS ARE REPORTED, NOT FORBIDDEN`): a module in no subsystem or whose subsystem's decision does not
  name it; a module that realises no requirement; an accepted requirement no module realises — accepted as its caller
  marks it —; a module no test exercises, or without code; a code file outside every module's folder, or a folder no
  module names; an import between modules that the importing module's file does not name among the interfaces it uses;
  a module folder inside another; a name that matches nothing. Where imports could not be read for a file's language,
  `importsRead` is false and the row says so.
- `compareGraphs(earlier: Graph, later: Graph) -> Comparison` — the requirements added, changed and removed between two
  versions, and the coverage gained and lost (UC-020).
- `selfSufficiencyFindings(graph: Graph, instance: string) -> Finding[]` — an error under `THE PRODUCT REPOSITORY IS
  SELF-SUFFICIENT` for each of the graph's `links` whose target is a path of the repository that `files` does not hold,
  the instance's repository `instance`, given as `owner/name`, or its dashboard at the address MOD-identifiers'
  `pagesAddress` gives it (`AN INSTANCE IS A FORK OF AGENT M`). MOD-job-runner's check `graph-checks` runs it on every draft.

## Files

It reads, through the `TextSource` it is given, the files listed under Data, and the files `<commit>.json` and
`<commit>.impacts.json` of the branch `trace-cache`. It writes both on that branch, only by adding, and only in
`publishGraph`.

## Uses

- `MOD-documents.artifactSchemas`, `MOD-documents.readDocument` and the type `MOD-documents.Document` — to read use cases,
  decisions, module files and items by their schemas.
- `MOD-identifiers.identifiersIn`, `MOD-identifiers.kindOfIdentifier`, `MOD-identifiers.positionalReferences` and the type
  `MOD-identifiers.IdentifierKind` — to find the identifiers and names a text writes, their kinds, and references by
  position; `MOD-identifiers.pagesAddress` — the instance's dashboard, which no artifact may link.
- `MOD-spec-document.parseSpec` and the type `MOD-spec-document.Spec` — to read the requirements.
- `MOD-test-document.isTestFile`, `MOD-test-document.testDeclarations` and the type `MOD-test-document.TestDeclaration` —
  to tell the test files and read their tests.
- `MOD-group-document.parseGroupFile` — to read the groups' titles.
- `MOD-text-tools.blobSha` — the blob of each node.
- `MOD-text-tools.finding` and the type `MOD-text-tools.Finding` — the findings it reports.
- `MOD-repository-hosts.Host`, `MOD-repository-hosts.Snapshot` and `MOD-repository-hosts.commitFiles` — `publishGraph`'s
  reading of the branch head and its one commit.

# MOD-trace-pages One trace page for every view over the trace graph

## Responsibility

It belongs to the Site (ARC-038). Its one responsibility is every view that reads the trace graph of one version of a
product, written once as a template method: choosing a version — the default branch or a release tag, and a second one
to compare —, showing a tree or a table, narrowing it by filters, opening a row, and following its links. A view takes
part through its **descriptor**. The views are the specification browser with each requirement's traces, proposals and
history; the coverage gaps; the modules view with its component diagram; the tests browser; and the audit of a release
with its export. Everything is derived when it is shown, from the artifacts of the chosen version; nothing is read from a
stored matrix (`THE TRACEABILITY MATRIX IS DERIVED`).

It serves UC-020, UC-025, UC-029 and UC-030, and gives the prompt bar the subject of what it shows (UC-049). Editing,
the draft of a change asked for in the prompt bar, and arranging are the review pages' routes, which its links lead to.

It runs in a browser, loaded by `docs/index.html` through MOD-site-frame.

## Parts

- `index.mjs` — the interface: `view`.
- `flow.mjs` — the template method: version choice and comparison, tree or table, filters, a row's detail, links.
- `subject.mjs` — the subject the specification view gives the prompt bar: what is open, its kind and draft route, the
  person's own source.
- `views.mjs` — the five descriptors.
- `diagram.mjs` — the component diagram of the modules view, as Mermaid.
- `tests.mjs` — the tests view: the tests of the version as a tree or grouped, their filters, the incomplete ones, and the comparison of two
  releases.
- `test-detail.mjs` — an opened test of the tests view: its declaration, schedule, counter-proof, code and history.
- `audit.mjs` — the audit view of a release: its summary, filters and rows.
- `export.mjs` — saving the audit document in the browser.
- **Taken over, outside this folder** (`CODE OUTSIDE THE ARCHITECTURE IS MOVED INTO IT`; the count in `docs/measurements/2026-10-17_code-outside-every-module.md`). Each file goes as stated, in this module's own implementation jobs:
  - `tests/trace-pages-edit-links.test.mjs`: its header names this module.

## Data

It keeps nothing but the screen. It owns the **descriptor** of a trace view:

```text
TraceView = {
  key: "specification" | "gaps" | "modules" | "tests" | "audit",
  entry: "requirements" | "architecture" | "tests" | "releases",   // the menu entry it is under
  versions: "branch-and-tags" | "tags",                            // what the version choice offers; a second version compares
  shape: "tree" | "table",
  rows: (graph, facts) -> Row[],                                   // built from the trace graph and the services' facts
  groupings: string[],                                             // the ways its rows can be grouped
  filters: Filter[],                                               // { name, values, keep(row) -> boolean }
  detail: (row, facts) -> Section[],                               // what opening a row shows
  links: (row) -> Link[],                                          // routes it leads to, its own or the review pages'
  extras: string[]                                                 // "component-diagram", "export"
}
```

| View | Versions | Shape and rows | Opening a row | Extras |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| specification | branch and tags | first, only while an entry of a change queue waits for acceptance, those entries, each with its status and a link to it (MOD-review-pages' `spec-entry/<id>`), and nothing where none waits; then the tree of `docs/groups/requirements.md`, every requirement once with its status — in SPEC, change proposed, removal proposed, proposed — and, where MOD-source-register's `affectedRequirements` names it for a source the product moved to a newer version after its section last changed, *source changed* until its section changes (UC-016 step 5), each group with how many it holds and how many no use case realises | the four fields; sources with version and part; use cases with their review status; decisions, modules and tests naming it; open proposals; its history of accepted changes | to the review pages, on the default branch only: *Edit* on a requirement, *+ Requirement* once for each section of the SPEC, listed beside the tree and not within it, each of which opens `requirements/new` for that section (UC-018 3d), and *Arrange*; *History of SPEC changes*, which opens MOD-review-pages' `spec-entry/history`. Its subject for the prompt bar, on the default branch, is the open requirement, or the group with the names it holds, with the kind `change-requirements`, the person's own source and the review pages' `draft` as its draft route (UC-019 step 1); at a released version, the requirement as it read there, with the kind `converse` (UC-020 1a, UC-049 2a) |
| gaps | branch and tags | table of requirements realised by no use case and named by no module or test, use cases realising none, names matching nothing | the artifact as it read in that version | what became covered and what lost its coverage between two versions |
| modules | branch | table of modules: subsystem, the requirements its tests guard with their statuses, its file, code, tests; and every gap | the module's file and folder | component diagram: one box per module in its subsystem's box, one arrow per use, gaps marked, a missing provider as a box marked *missing*; *Change the architecture* and *Implement* |
| tests | branch and tags | tree by level, file and case, or by requirement, use case or module, each test with its outcome on the latest commit | its declaration, its schedule, its counter-proof, its code, its history across commits and releases | comparing two releases |
| audit | tags | one row per requirement valid at the tag, with a summary at the top | the guarding tests with outcomes or rates and counter-proofs, process gates, the acceptance of the report | *Export* as one Markdown document; *Commit export* |

## Interfaces

- `view: View` — the routes of the five trace views, `trace/<key>`, each with its version and filters in its `params`,
  and `trace/<key>/<row>` for an opened row, each with its subject for the prompt bar: the specification view's as its
  descriptor says, every other view's the frame's default with the version shown among its page; its strategies are
  none, since it starts no job itself.

## Files

It writes one file, and only on a person's click: the audit document under `docs/audits/<tag>.md` (*Commit export*).
It reads the product's snapshot at the chosen version through its host — the SPEC, the group files, use cases,
architecture files, code files, tests, approval records, the product's links to sources —, the history of the SPEC and
the result records on the branch `test-results`. For the audit it reads the product's `docs/process.md` and `docs/gates/`
at the release's commit, and the instance's `SPEC.md`, whose requirements are the process requirements. Through the
instance's host that the frame gives every route, it also reads the instance's process models at the commit that this
`docs/process.md` names (`model_version`), for the model the product had declared at the release (UC-031 6a).

A mark of an opened test's history (UC-029 step 5) finds the id of its run in the `run` address of the result records of its
commit on the branch `test-results` that hold the test: the last part of the address's path, as `WebLinks`' `run` builds it
(`…/actions/runs/<id>` on GitHub, `…/-/pipelines/<id>` on GitLab); a mark whose records name no run has no link to a log.
The link to the full log is `WebLinks`' `run` for that id; where `ciRunLog` gives `null` for it, the server no longer keeps the
log, the link reads *no longer available*, and the mark keeps its outcome (UC-029 5b).

## Uses

- MOD-site-frame.View, MOD-site-frame.chosenProduct, MOD-site-frame.explain, MOD-site-frame.notice, MOD-site-frame.readProblem,
  MOD-site-frame.confirmDecision — the frame's parts of every route.
- MOD-markdown-render.renderArtifact, MOD-markdown-render.renderMermaid, MOD-markdown-render.showDifference — rows'
  details, the component diagram, the comparison of versions.
- MOD-repository-hosts.readSnapshot, MOD-repository-hosts.readHistory, MOD-repository-hosts.readFileAt,
  MOD-repository-hosts.listTags,
  MOD-repository-hosts.webLinks — the version, the history of a requirement's section, the text of a file at the commits
  of its history, the release tags, a test's code (`WebLinks`' `file`, the page of the test's file at the version shown)
  and a run's log on the server; for the audit, the instance at the commit the release's declaration names;
  MOD-repository-hosts.repositoryInfo — the default branch, on which alone a requirement leads to editing, and at which
  the instance's links are read for the person's own source; MOD-repository-hosts.ciRunLog — whether the server still keeps a
  run's log (UC-029 5b).
- MOD-documents.artifactSchemas, MOD-documents.readDocument, MOD-spec-document.parseSpec, MOD-group-document.parseGroupFile,
  MOD-group-document.hierarchy, MOD-test-document.testDeclarations — the artifacts of the version.
- MOD-trace-graph.traceGraph, MOD-trace-graph.tracesTo, MOD-trace-graph.coverageGaps, MOD-trace-graph.compareGraphs,
  MOD-trace-graph.moduleRows, MOD-trace-graph.graphFindings — the rows, gaps, unknown names and comparisons.
- MOD-approvals.statuses — the review status of use cases and architecture files.
- MOD-spec-changes.queues, MOD-spec-changes.entryView, MOD-spec-changes.requirementHistory — open proposals, what each
  open entry changes, withdraws or adds (its `impact`), and a requirement's history.
- MOD-source-register.sourceSchemas, MOD-source-register.linkedVersion — a requirement's sources with version and part;
  MOD-source-register.affectedRequirements — the requirements marked *source changed*;
  MOD-source-register.personSource, MOD-source-register.personAccount — the person's own source, which the subject of a
  requirement carries.
- MOD-prompt-bar.Subject — the subject each route gives the prompt bar.
- MOD-test-schedule.occasionsOf — when the schedule runs a test; MOD-test-schedule.scheduleSchema reads the product's
  `docs/tests/schedule.md` at the version shown, and MOD-test-schedule.defaultSchedule gives the book's schedule where the
  product has none, the document `occasionsOf` is given.
- MOD-result-records.resultsAt, MOD-result-records.flakyTests, MOD-result-records.rateComparison,
  MOD-result-records.testHistory — outcomes, flaky tests, rates and history; MOD-result-records.resultSchema reads a
  test's counter-proof record, whose `participant` is shown as the one who wrote the test.
- MOD-release-evidence.auditRows, MOD-release-evidence.auditDocument — the audit and its document; the audit is given the
  instance's SPEC, where the process requirements stand.
- MOD-product-process.declarationSchema, productWorkflow, gateSchema, gateStates — the product's workflow and its gate
  records at the release's commit, from which the audit's process rows take each process requirement's gates and records
  (UC-030). The workflow is `productWorkflow` of the declaration at the release, so it is derived from the model the
  product had declared then.
- MOD-artifact-edits.saveFile — *Commit export*, as the person's own input.

# MOD-tunnels The Bridge's own SSH key and its tunnels to the jump host

## Responsibility

It belongs to the Bridge (ARC-040). It opens and keeps the SSH connections a Bridge needs when a computer behind NAT is to
be reached (UC-011, UC-044): the reverse tunnel from that computer to the jump host, bound to the jump host's loopback
only (`A BRIDGE BEHIND NAT IS REACHED THROUGH A REVERSE TUNNEL`, `A REVERSE TUNNEL LISTENS ONLY ON THE JUMP HOST'S
LOOPBACK`), and the matching forward on the person's own computer — so that nobody types an SSH command (`THE BRIDGE OPENS
ITS TUNNELS ITSELF`). It makes and keeps the Bridge's own key pair (`THE BRIDGE CREATES ITS OWN SSH KEY`). It speaks SSH
with the ssh2 package inside the Bridge's process (ARC-052). It runs in Node, in the Bridge's main process.

## Parts

- `index.mjs` — the interface.
- `key.mjs` — the key pair.
- `tunnel.mjs` — one tunnel: connecting, forwarding, keeping alive, reopening.
- `handlers.mjs` — the `tunnels` route of the Bridge's API.

## Data

Files in the Bridge's per-user data folder, outside every repository:

- `ssh/id_ed25519` — the private key, made on first use, readable and writable by its owner only; it never leaves the
  computer and is part of no export.
- `ssh/id_ed25519.pub` — the public key, shown in the Bridge's window to be added to `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` of the
  jump host's user.
- `ssh/known-jump-hosts` — the host key of each jump host, kept from the first connection; a jump host that later shows
  another key is refused.

The tunnels themselves are read from the plans the Bridge's settings hold, in the format MOD-bridge-client defines
(`TunnelPlan`); their states live in memory.

## Interfaces

- `ensureKey(dataFolder: string) -> Promise<{ publicKey: string, fingerprint: string }>` — the Bridge's key pair, made
  the first time it is needed, an Ed25519 pair, its private key written readable by its owner only. Errors: `NotWritable`
  with the folder.
- `openTunnels(dataFolder: string, plans: TunnelPlan[], bridgePort: number) -> Promise<void>` — opens every tunnel of the
  plans and keeps it open: a reverse tunnel asks the jump host to listen on its loopback address at the plan's port and
  carries each connection there to the Bridge's own port on loopback; a forward listens on this computer's loopback at the
  plan's port and carries each connection to the jump host's loopback at the same port. Each connection sends SSH
  keepalives and is reopened after sleep or a change of network, with growing waits. It refuses a plan whose bind
  address on the jump host is not its loopback, with `NotLoopback`. Crosses the network to the jump host; a tunnel that
  cannot be opened does not stop the others, and its state says why.
- `closeTunnels() -> Promise<void>` — closes every tunnel, on pause, quit or a changed plan.
- `tunnelState() -> { name: string, kind: "reverse" | "forward", state: "open" | "opening" | "closed" | "failed", reason:
  string | null }[]` — each tunnel's state; the reasons are `auth-refused` — the jump host does not accept the Bridge's key;
  the window shows the public key again and what to do with it —, `host-unreachable`, `host-key-changed` — the jump host
  shows another key than the one kept; nothing is sent to it —, and `port-taken` — another session holds the port on the
  jump host.
- `tunnelHandlers` — the handler of the `tunnels` route of `bridgeApi`, of MOD-bridge-http's type `BridgeHandlers`: the
  states of `tunnelState`.

## Files

Reads and writes `ssh/id_ed25519`, `ssh/id_ed25519.pub` and `ssh/known-jump-hosts` in the Bridge's per-user data folder.
Writes no repository file.

## Uses

- `MOD-bridge-http.bridgeApi`, `MOD-bridge-http.BridgeHandlers` — the route it answers.
- `MOD-bridge-client.TunnelPlan` — the plan of a tunnel, the same the dashboard turns into commands for a computer
  without a Bridge, so both ends agree.

# MOD-work-plans Implementation plans, backlogs and sprints, and the state of each item

## Responsibility

It belongs to Process (ARC-042). It keeps the work of a product: the implementation plan of a model that plans its work,
in its order (`THE IMPLEMENTATION PLAN LIVES IN THE PRODUCT REPOSITORY`, `AN IMPLEMENTATION PLAN ASSEMBLES THE SYSTEM FROM
ITS MODULES`, `A PLAN STEP NAMES THE TESTS OF ITS LEVEL`), and the backlog and sprints of a model that pulls its work
(`THE BACKLOG LIVES IN THE PRODUCT REPOSITORY`, `A BACKLOG ITEM NAMES WHAT IT REALISES`, `A BACKLOG ITEM NAMES THE MODULES IT
CHANGES`). A backlog keeps no order of its own: its items are listed after the items they build on. In a model with
sprints, every team runs sprints of its own, and a sprint holds its items until their change is in the default branch or
they return to the backlog. A team's selection is refused when one of its items changes a module that an item of another
team's sprint changes or uses, or uses a module that such an item changes (`EVERY TEAM RUNS SPRINTS OF ITS OWN`, `A SPRINT
HOLDS ITS ITEMS UNTIL THEY REACH THE DEFAULT BRANCH`, `SPRINTS OF DIFFERENT TEAMS CHANGE NO MODULE THE OTHER CHANGES OR
USES`, `SPRINT PLANNING SHOWS WHAT THE OTHER TEAMS' SPRINTS HOLD`). It derives each step's or item's state and every reason
it cannot start (`NOTHING IS IMPLEMENTED BEFORE IT IS ACCEPTED`, `NO JOB STARTS ABOVE THE WORK-IN-PROGRESS LIMIT`, `A TIME
BOX WORKS ONLY ON WHAT WAS SELECTED FOR IT`), never storing a state (`PROGRESS AND JOB STATE ARE DERIVED, NOT STORED`), and
records a sprint from its start to its review and retrospective (`A SPRINT ENDS WITH A REVIEW OF ITS INCREMENT`, `A SPRINT
ENDS WITH A RETROSPECTIVE`). It commits each save of a plan, of items, and of a sprint's start, end and close as one commit
on the head that was read, checked by its findings — a person's own input on the page, and the same functions behind the
writers of the kinds that draft a plan, propose items and close a sprint, whose recipes and checks it offers too. It runs
in the browser and in Node.

## Parts

- `index.mjs` — the interface.
- `plan-order.schema.md`, `sprint.schema.md` — the schemas, in MOD-documents' schema language.
- `states.mjs` — item states and startability.
- `checks.mjs` — the findings of a plan and of a backlog.
- `sprints.mjs` — the facts of a sprint, the items the sprints hold, and what keeps an item from a team's selection.
- `saves.mjs` — the commits of a plan, of items and of a sprint.
- `strategies.mjs` — the recipes, checks and writers of `workStrategies`.
- **Taken over, outside this folder** (`CODE OUTSIDE THE ARCHITECTURE IS MOVED INTO IT`; the count in `docs/measurements/2026-10-17_code-outside-every-module.md`). Each file goes as stated, in this module's own implementation jobs:
  - `docs/assets/work-items.mjs`, `docs/assets/work-items/flow.mjs`: removed once no file imports them.
  - `tests/test_backlog_layout.py`, `tests/test_backlog_item_fields.py`, `tests/release-sprint-02-b-work-items.test.mjs`, `tests/flow_fixture.py`, `tests/test_job_from_backlog.py`, `tests/test_time_box_selection.py`, `tests/test_wip_limit.py`, `tests/test_implementation_job.py`, `tests/test_job_preconditions.py`: their headers name this module; one of only the old items is rewritten on this module.

## Data

It keeps nothing. It owns two formats; the files of the steps and items themselves (`ITM-<nnn>-<slug>.md`) are of the
item schema of MOD-documents (`artifactSchemas().item`).

| Schema | File | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `plan-order` | `docs/plan/order.md` | a table `Step`, `Phase`: every step of the plan by identifier, in its order, with the phase of the model it belongs to |
| `sprint` | `docs/backlog/sprints/<team>/<nn>.md`, numbered within the team; `<team>` is the name of the team's role assignment | front matter `sprint`, `goal`, `start`, `end` (the date the time box gives, empty without one), `closer` (the participant who closes it), `branch` (its own branch, empty for none), `selection` (the items); then sections appended as the sprint goes on, never rewritten: `## Selection` when the selection is changed by a new start decision, `## Ended` when the Product Owner ends a sprint without a time box, `## Increment given up` (`at:`, `by:` the Product Owner, `reason:`) when the Product Owner gives up an increment that was not merged, `## Review` (the increment, the items not done with their reasons, each feedback line with where it goes — new item, change to an item, noted —, who took part, and for an agent the sources of its feedback), `## Unfinished items` (each to the backlog or into the next sprint, with the reason), `## Retrospective` (what went well, what did not, each change with where it goes — process model, Definition of Done, a participant's instructions, team agreement —; an agent's changes as proposals only) |

An item's state, `ItemState`, is derived from the approval records, the queues, the job records and the pull requests:
`waiting for acceptance`, `waiting for an item it builds on`, `ready`, `in progress` (a job runs, or its pull request is
open; and once its newest job has ended as done, until a pull request of it opened after that job's `start` is merged or
closed without merge), `blocked` (a job failed, or waits for a person), `done` (its pull request is merged). A plan step
that waits for the gate before its phase is `waiting` with that gate named.

An item is held by a team's sprint from its selection until a pull request with its change is merged into the default
branch, or until its sprint's close sends it back to the backlog or into the team's next sprint: once the close is recorded
— its record holds `## Review` —, the sprint holds none of its items without a merged pull request. Once its record also
holds `## Increment given up`, it holds none of its items at all, and its done items are back in the backlog (UC-041 7b). An item's role
assignment is the one of the team whose sprint holds it, and the product's one in a model without sprints.

## Interfaces

- `ItemState` — `{ item: string, state: "waiting for acceptance" | "waiting for an item it builds on" | "waiting" |
  "ready" | "in progress" | "blocked" | "done" | "unknown", reason: string | null, job: string | null, pullRequest:
  string | null }`; `unknown` when the state needs pull requests the host could not read; `job` the newest job whose
  record works on the item, also once that job has ended, and null when there is none.
- `Held` — `{ item: string, sprint: string, team: string, changes: string[], uses: string[] }`: an item a team's sprint
  holds, with the modules it changes and the modules whose interfaces those use.
- `planSchemas: { planOrder: Schema, sprint: Schema }` — the two schemas, for MOD-documents and
  for the page's forms.
- `itemStates(items: Document[], order: Document | null, facts: { statuses: Map<string, { id: string, kind: string, status:
  string }>, queues: Queue[], jobs: JobRow[], pullRequests: PullRequest[] | "unknown", gates: Array<{ gate: string,
  state: string }>, workflow: Workflow | null }) -> ItemState[]` — every step in the plan's order, or every item after the items it builds on — a backlog has no
  `order` —, with its state, from
  the approval statuses, the change queues, the jobs, the pull requests and the gate states `gateStates` gives; with the
  pull requests `"unknown"` — a host that does no server operations —, a step or item whose state needs them is
  `unknown`, never guessed; a requirement an item realises that has been withdrawn or changed marks the item.
- `startable(item: string, states: ItemState[], context: { workflow: Workflow, assignment: Document, sprint: Document |
  null, held: Held[], wip: number | null, participants: Participant[] }) -> { startable: true } | { startable: false,
  reasons: string[] }` — every reason a job for this step or item cannot start: not selected for the current sprint of its
  team, `sprint`; a requirement or use case it names not accepted, named; an item it builds on not done, named; the
  work-in-progress limit reached by the items in progress under `assignment`, the item's role assignment, naming them and
  those waiting for review; the gate before its phase not recorded, naming it and its decider; no holder of the
  implementing role in `assignment` with what the role needs.
- `heldItems(sprints: Document[], items: Document[], architecture: Document[], pullRequests: PullRequest[] | "unknown",
  onDefault?: Set<string>) -> Held[]` — every item a team's sprint holds, from the sprint records and the pull requests,
  with the modules it changes and the modules whose interfaces they use (`A SPRINT HOLDS ITS ITEMS UNTIL THEY REACH THE
  DEFAULT BRANCH`); with the pull requests unknown, a selected item counts as held. An item's hold ends when a merged pull
  request naming it reaches the default branch through the pull requests that merge its base on, or when that pull
  request's head commit is in `onDefault` — the head commits a caller found on the default branch with the host's
  `containsCommit`, for a change that reached it another way. Without `onDefault`, only the pull requests decide.
- `undecidedHeads(sprints: Document[], pullRequests: PullRequest[]) -> string[]` — the head commits of the merged pull
  requests that name an item a sprint holds and whose chain of pull requests reaches no default branch: the only commits a
  caller needs to ask `containsCommit` about before calling `heldItems`. Pure; no request.
- `conflicts(item: Document, team: string, held: Held[], architecture: Document[]) -> Array<{ sprint: string, team:
  string, item: string, module: string }>` — what keeps an item from the team's selection: each item another team's sprint
  holds that is the item itself, changes a module the item changes or uses, or uses a module the item changes, with that
  module (`SPRINTS OF DIFFERENT TEAMS CHANGE NO MODULE THE OTHER CHANGES OR USES`).
- `planFindings(plan: Document, steps: Document[], architecture: Document[], workflow: Workflow, source: TextSource,
  history?: { host: Host }, graph?: Graph) -> Promise<Finding[]>` — a module, a subsystem or the system without a step; with `history`, a
  step whose module or subsystem file was removed, and a step whose module or subsystem file was changed by a commit later
  than the step's own last commit (`readHistory` of both files, `changes: false`), each naming the file and the step, so
  that the plan page marks them after an architecture change (UC-045); a module ordered before one whose interface
  it uses; a step without a phase of the model; and the findings MOD-trace-graph's `graphFindings` gives on
  `traceGraph(source)`, `source` being the product's files with the drafted steps in place, of those steps: a step
  without the tests of its level, or with the tests of another, and a cycle in the modules' uses, naming its modules.
  `graph`, the graph `traceGraph` gives, is passed only by a caller whose steps are the commit's own — the plan page,
  with the graph it asked for with its commit —; `graphFindings` then runs on it and `source` is read for no
  graph. Without `graph`, the graph is built from `source`, as above. Crosses the network through `source` for the
  files it has not read; fails with its errors.
- `backlogFindings(items: Document[], architecture: Document[]) -> Finding[]` — an item that realises nothing; that names
  no module the architecture describes; that builds on an item that does not exist, or on one that builds on it in turn;
  and, as a warning, an item that restates an existing one.
- `sprintFacts(sprint: Document, facts: { items: Document[], tests: Array<{ id: string, guards: string[] }>, states:
  ItemState[], jobs: JobRow[], results: Snapshot, pullRequests: PullRequest[], issues: Issue[] }) -> { increment: Array<{ item: string, pullRequest: string, realises: string[],
  tests: string[] }>, notDone: ItemState[], numbers: { failedJobs: number, retriedJobs: number, correctionRounds: number,
  waitingAtGates: string, waitingForAPerson: string, flakyTests: string[], cost: string } }` — the sprint's increment,
  what is not done and why, and the numbers of the sprint, each derived; `items` are the backlog items or plan steps, from
  which an item's `realises` come, and `tests` the tests of the product with the requirements each guards, so that an
  item's tests are those that guard a requirement it realises; `results` is the branch `test-results`; a cost
  only where a job's row has one (`NO COST IS GUESSED`).
- `targetBranch(item: string, context: { sprints: Document[], order: Document | null, branches: Record<string,
  string>, defaultBranch: string }) -> string` — the branch a plan step's or backlog item's work is merged into: the
  `branch` of the sprint whose current selection names it and whose record holds neither `## Review` nor `## Increment
  given up`, where that record names one; else the branch `branches` gives the step's phase in `order`; else
  `defaultBranch` (`A PHASE OR A TIME BOX MAY HAVE A BRANCH OF ITS OWN`, `WORK MERGES INTO THE DEFAULT BRANCH
  UNLESS A BRANCH IS SET`). `branches` is the declaration's `## Branches` as MOD-product-process' `branchesOf` gives
  it. It reads nothing.
- `sprintsToClose(sprints: Document[], states: ItemState[], today: string) -> Array<{ sprint: string, closer: string,
  because: "time box ended" | "every selected item done" | "ended by the Product Owner" }>` — every sprint whose record
  holds no `## Review` and that has ended: its `end` date is before or on `today`; or, without a time box, every item of
  its selection is `done`, or its record holds `## Ended`; each with its `closer` (UC-041, an agent's close; `A SPRINT
  CLOSED BY AN AGENT STARTS BY ITSELF`). It reads nothing.
- `savePlan(host: Host, plan: { steps: Document[], order: Document, removed: string[] }, context: { architecture:
  Document[], workflow: Workflow, head: string, trailers: string[] }) -> Promise<{ commit: string, written: string[] }>` —
  **Save plan** (UC-045): `planFindings` first, and with an error finding nothing is written; a new step gets an
  identifier that no history of `docs/plan/` and `docs/backlog/` holds; one commit of one file per step under
  `docs/plan/` and `docs/plan/order.md`, the files of removed steps deleted. `trailers` are a job's provenance lines,
  empty for a person's own input — the same for every save below. Crosses the network. Errors: `PlanRefused { findings
  }`, `Moved`, `TokenRefused`, `PermissionMissing`, `RateLimited`, `Unreachable` — the host's errors, here and below.
- `saveItems(host: Host, change: { items: Document[], removed: string[] }, context: { architecture:
  Document[], head: string, trailers: string[] }) -> Promise<{ commit: string, written: string[], warnings: Finding[] }>`
  — **Add to backlog** and **+ Item** (UC-032), an item pointed at a replacing requirement or removed (UC-032 1a), and
  **Move to backlog** (UC-033): `backlogFindings` first, and with an error finding nothing is written; a warning — an item
  that restates an existing one — is returned with the commit; a new item gets an identifier that no history holds; one
  commit of the item files under `docs/backlog/`. An item added while a sprint runs enters the backlog, never the
  sprint's selection. Errors: `ItemsRefused { findings }`, and
  the host's.
- `startSprint(host: Host, sprint: { team: string, goal: string, start: string, closer: string, selection: string[] },
  context: { states: ItemState[], model: Model, declaration: Document, held: Held[], architecture: Document[], running:
  Document | null, head: string, trailers: string[] }) -> Promise<{ commit: string, path: string, added: string[],
  removed: string[] }>` — **Start sprint** (UC-032 step 6), for one team: `end` set to the date the model's time box gives
  from `start`, empty without one; `branch` the one the declaration gives the time box, its placeholders `<team>` and
  `<nn>` filled with the team and its next number, created from the head where it does not exist yet; `docs/backlog/sprints/<team>/<nn>.md` committed with the team's next
  number. `held` is read at the head the commit is written on, and each selected item is checked with `conflicts` (UC-032
  6c). While a sprint runs, a new start decision is appended to its file as `## Selection`, and `added` and `removed` name
  what it changes (UC-032 6a). Errors: `SprintRefused { reasons }` — an item waiting for acceptance, one selected without
  the items it builds on that are not done, or one that `conflicts` names, with the sprint, the held item and the module
  —, and the host's.
- `endSprint(host: Host, sprint: string, context: { head: string, now: Date, trailers: string[] }) -> Promise<{ commit:
  string }>` — **End sprint** (UC-032 6b): appends `## Ended` with the date to a sprint without a time box. Errors:
  `NotFound { path }` for a sprint with no record, `NotEndable` for a sprint with a time box, whose end is its date, or one
  already ended — nothing is written in either case —; and the host's.
- `closeSprint(host: Host, close: { sprint: string, review: { feedback: Array<{ line: string, goes: "new item" | "change
  to an item" | "noted", item: string | null }>, tookPart: string[], sources: string[] | null }, unfinished: Array<{ item:
  string, to: "backlog" | "next sprint", reason: string }>, retrospective: Array<{ text: string, kind: "went well" | "did
  not go well" | "change", goes: "process model" | "Definition of Done" | "a participant's instructions" | "team
  agreement" | null }>, newItems: Document[] }, context: { facts: ReturnType<typeof sprintFacts>, architecture:
  Document[], head: string, trailers: string[] }) -> Promise<{ commit: string, written: string[] }>` —
  **Close sprint** (UC-041 step 6): appends `## Review` — the increment and the items not done from `facts`, the feedback,
  who took part, for an agent the sources of its feedback —, `## Unfinished items` and `## Retrospective` to the sprint's
  file; adds the feedback's new items to the backlog as `saveItems` does, and records for each unfinished item whether it
  goes back to the backlog or into the team's next sprint; all in one commit. Errors: `NotFound { path }` for a sprint with no record, `RetrospectiveMissing` (UC-041 6a), `Undecided { items }` for an unfinished item
  without a decision, `AlreadyClosed`, `ItemsRefused { findings }`, and the host's.
- `giveUpIncrement(host: Host, sprint: string, reason: string, context: { head: string, trailers: string[] }) -> Promise<{
  commit: string }>` — the Product Owner's *Give up increment* for a closed sprint whose branch was not merged: appends
  `## Increment given up` with the date, the person and the reason, in one commit; the sprint then holds none of its items
  (UC-041 7b). Errors: `NotFound { path }`, `NotClosed` for a sprint without `## Review`, `Merged` for a sprint whose
  branch's pull request is merged, and the host's.
- `workStrategies: Strategies` — the strategies this module offers the job runner (ARC-046):
  - recipe `architecture-and-model` — the decision that states the system, the subsystems' decisions, the module files,
    the process model with its phases and gates, and the existing plan;
  - recipe `backlog-inputs` — the accepted requirements and use cases, those no item realises yet, the architecture, and
    the existing items, which its part carries as artifacts keyed by their title;
  - recipe `sprint-facts` — the sprint's facts, the product's issues opened or closed during the sprint, its job records
    and result records — each named as a source; never a mail. The sprint is the one the job's parameter `sprint` names;
    its facts are `sprintFacts` of the product's items, of its tests with what each guards (`isTestFile`,
    `testDeclarations`), of the items' states (`itemStates`, with the product's workflow), of its jobs (`listJobs`,
    without live states), of the branch `test-results` (the product host's `readSnapshot`), of its pull requests, and of
    the issues whose `opened` or `closed` falls within the sprint; where the product's host gives no issues, they are
    left out and named as not read;
  - check `plan-checks` — `planFindings` on a drafted plan, with the product's workflow and no `graph`, since its steps
    are drafted; where the product has no workflow, one error finding naming the declared model and its commit;
  - check `backlog-checks` — `backlogFindings` on drafted items;
  - check `sprint-record-checks` — an agent's review that does not name the sources of its feedback, or does not say that
    no stakeholder took part when none did (`AN AGENT'S REVIEW NAMES WHERE ITS FEEDBACK CAME FROM`); a retrospective
    without an entry; a change to the process written as applied rather than proposed (`AN AGENT'S RETROSPECTIVE CHANGES
    NO PROCESS BY ITSELF`);
  - writer `plan-steps` — the drafted plan through `savePlan`, with the job's provenance lines;
  - writer `backlog-items` — the drafted items through `saveItems`, with the job's provenance lines;
  - writer `sprint-record` — an agent's close through `closeSprint`, with the job's provenance lines, under the closer's
    name; the proposals of the retrospective stay proposals.

`Workflow` is MOD-product-process'; `Model` MOD-model-catalogue's; `Queue` MOD-spec-changes'; `JobRow` MOD-job-ledger's;
`Participant` MOD-participant-list's; `Schema` and `Document` MOD-documents'; `Host`, `Snapshot`, `PullRequest` and
`Issue` MOD-repository-hosts'.

## Files

- Reads `docs/plan/`, `docs/backlog/`, `docs/backlog/sprints/`, `docs/process.md` through the workflow, the role
  assignments under `docs/role-assignments/`, the architecture
  under `docs/architecture/`, `SPEC.md`, the approval records, the change queues, `docs/jobs/`, the branch `test-results`,
  the pull requests and the issues of the product, and the history of `docs/plan/` and `docs/backlog/`.
- Writes, through its saves, `docs/plan/ITM-*.md`, `docs/plan/order.md`, `docs/backlog/ITM-*.md` and
  `docs/backlog/sprints/<team>/<nn>.md`, and creates a sprint's own branch.

## Uses

- MOD-product-process.Workflow, gateStates, holdsRole — the phases and gates, a gate's state, the implementing role's
  holders in a role assignment; MOD-product-process.productWorkflow — the product's workflow in a job, of its
  declaration `docs/process.md`, the instance read through its host's `readSnapshot`, and the instance's SPEC, for
  `plan-checks` and `sprint-facts`.
- MOD-model-catalogue.Model — the phases a plan's steps belong to.
- MOD-approvals.statuses, MOD-spec-changes.Queue, queues, MOD-spec-document.parseSpec — whether what an item names is
  accepted.
- MOD-trace-graph.systemDecisions — the decisions of the system and of its subsystems, for `architecture-and-model`.
- MOD-trace-graph.graphFindings, TextSource — the findings of a drafted plan's steps that the graph's checks give, on a
  source of the product's files with the drafted steps in place.
